motivation: The work aims to establish when module categories of vertex operator algebras are rigid braided ribbon categories or modular tensor categories under cofiniteness and self-contragredience assumptions.
method: It introduces a moderate-growth condition for objects in abelian pivotal braided r-categories using the Grothendieck-Verdier duality functor, then applies this to grading-restricted generalized modules over vertex operator algebras.
result: Under suitable conditions, the category of C2-cofinite grading-restricted generalized modules is shown to be a locally finite rigid braided ribbon category, and for Z-graded self-contragredient C2-cofinite vertex operator algebras the category of all grading-restricted generalized modules is a modular tensor category.
conclusion: The paper is a pure mathematics contribution to vertex operator algebras and tensor category theory, with no direct connection to the user's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems interests.

title: Quadratic Apn Functions Of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ With A Self-Equivalence Of Prime Order
authors: Emanuele Bellini
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions of [MATH] have the lowest possible differential uniformity. The only known APN permutation in even dimension, in dimension six, is equivalent to a quadratic APN function with a nontrivial linear self-equivalence; no APN permutation is known for even [MATH]. In a published collection of about 3.8 million quadratic APN classes of dimension eight, at most 0.34% have a nontrivial linear self-equivalence. In dimension ten, the 25 literature classes considered here all have one. We study all quadratic APN functions of [MATH] with such a self-equivalence, which usually confines them to a much smaller linear space. Up to conjugacy and power similarity, self-equivalences of prime order have 299 types. We settle 298 of them. Elementary lemmas exclude 280 types, and exhaustive searches confirm this for 242 of them. The other 18 types are settled by exhaustive searches with exact equivalence certificates. Up to extended affine equivalence, the 298 types contain 29 classes of quadratic APN functions, four of them new. This also classifies the quadratic APN functions with coefficients in a subfield. Exactly 24 classes contain one with coefficients in [MATH], and all 3 that contain one with coefficients in [MATH] are among them. The open type consists of the quadratic canonical triplicate functions. They correspond to maximum additive Hermitian rank-distance codes. Three different searches find only the invariants of 16 classes, all among the 29. We conjecture there are no others. No quadratic APN function in the 298 settled types is Carlet-Charpin-Zinoviev equivalent to a permutation.
tldr: The paper classifies all quadratic almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions on F_2^10 admitting a linear self-equivalence of prime order, settling 298 of 299 conjugacy/power-similarity types and identifying 29 EA-equivalence classes, four of which are new.
motivation: APN functions have minimal differential uniformity and are central to constructing S-boxes resistant to differential cryptanalysis; the only known APN permutation in even dimension (dimension six) is equivalent to a quadratic APN function with nontrivial linear self-equivalence, motivating a systematic study of self-equivalences in dimension ten where no APN permutation is known.
method: Self-equivalences of prime order are enumerated up to conjugacy and power similarity, yielding 299 types; 280 are excluded by elementary lemmas (242 verified by exhaustive search), and 18 are settled by exhaustive searches with exact equivalence certificates, while the remaining type is linked to quadratic canonical triplicate functions and maximum additive Hermitian rank-distance codes.
result: The 298 settled types contain 29 EA-equivalence classes of quadratic APN functions (four new), exactly 24 classes have representatives with coefficients in a subfield and all 3 with a further subfield restriction are among them; no quadratic APN function in these types is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation, and the single open type is conjectured to yield no additional invariants beyond 16 known classes.
conclusion: The work provides a near-complete classification of a structured family of quadratic APN functions in dimension ten, closing most self-equivalence types and offering evidence (via conjecture) that the remaining triplicate case contributes nothing new.

title: Deterministic Ecdsa On Secp256k1: The Rfc 6979 Assumption, A Counterexample, And The State Of Deployed Implementations
authors: Ilia Prosianoi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: RFC 6979 derives the ECDSA nonce as [MATH], with [MATH] HMAC_DRBG keyed by the signing key x. We isolate the assumption its security rests on, A*: at known public key [MATH], the signing transcript under nonces [MATH] is indistinguishable from the transcript under uniform nonces. A* suffices, and it is neither PRF security of HMAC nor auxiliary-input PRF security (AI-PRF) of [MATH]. A function [MATH] is a PRF under standard assumptions yet leaks x from one signature; the same holds for unmodified RFC 6979 over a compression function that keeps the PRF and dual-PRF properties used in proofs of HMAC, given a collision-resistance premise. A* and AI-PRF are separated in both directions. A* does not imply AI-PRF if the one-bit hidden number problem is hard. Conversely, in the standard model: any AI-PRF can be modified so that it stays one while two chosen-digest signing queries reveal x; under DDH with one public random point, or decisional square Diffie-Hellman without it, there is an AI-PRF whose key is recovered from signatures on two ordinary hashed messages; and a third function, under PRF security and DLP, violates A* while the scheme stays unforgeable. With an ideal compression function, A* follows tightly from DLP in the presence of a randomized-ECDSA signing oracle, and a nonce key independent of x removes the assumption. The secret HMAC message block is [MATH] from uniform on secp256k1, [MATH] on P-256 and 0.336 on brainpoolP256r1. An audit of 31 secp256k1 implementations finds that 28 sign deterministically without added entropy and that the raw-message deviation from bits2octets of libsecp256k1 before 0.2.0 survives in NBitcoin, dcrd and btcec v2. Low-R grinding needs no assumption beyond A*, and every nonzero Fourier coefficient of the low-R nonce set is below [MATH] unconditionally. We give test vectors for the untested [MATH] branch.
tldr: The paper isolates and analyzes the cryptographic assumption (A*) underlying RFC 6979 deterministic ECDSA nonce derivation, constructs counterexamples separating it from PRF/AI-PRF notions, and audits 31 deployed secp256k1 implementations.
motivation: RFC 6979 is widely deployed, yet the precise security assumption its nonce derivation rests on had not been isolated, leaving a gap between informal proofs and actual guarantees.
method: Formal separation results via constructed PRF/AI-PRF counterexamples under standard assumptions (DDH, DLP), a tight reduction from DLP with an ideal compression function, statistical distance computations of the secret HMAC block, and an implementation audit of 31 secp256k1 libraries.
result: A* is shown to be strictly weaker than AI-PRF and neither implied by nor implying standard PRF notions; 28 of 31 implementations sign deterministically without added entropy, and a raw-message deviation persists in NBitcoin, dcrd and btcec v2.
conclusion: The security of deterministic ECDSA depends on a bespoke assumption that must be stated explicitly, and a nonce key independent of the signing key removes the assumption entirely.

title: An Inverse-Designed Multilayer Selective Emitter For High-Efficiency Thermophotovoltaics
authors: Md Anwar Hosen, Kavyashree Keremane, Bed Poudel, Linxiao Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High thermophotovoltaic (TPV) conversion efficiencies have typically relied on photovoltaic cells that reflect sub-bandgap radiation back toward the emitter. Here, we numerically investigate an alternative approach in which spectral selectivity is engineered primarily on the emitter side. We optimize an emitter consisting of 16-layer aperiodic MgO/Si coating on tungsten, for coupling to a GaSb cell with an antireflection coating and an Au mirror. A detailed-balance framework incorporates polarization- and angle-resolved emissivity, multiple reflections, and Auger nonradiative recombination. At an emitter temperature of 1500 K, the optimized structure suppresses 97.1% of the incident-blackbody-equivalent sub-bandgap power at the source; a further 1.9% is returned to the emitter by the cell, leaving 1.0% absorbed parasitically in the cell. The resulting modeled radiative-to-electrical conversion efficiency reaches 47.0%, compared with 30.8% for a SiC emitter paired with the same cell, while maintaining a comparable maximum electrical power density. These findings indicate that emitter-side spectral engineering could substantially relax cell-side photon-recycling requirements and provide significant improvement in TPV conversion.
tldr: A numerical study optimizing a 16-layer aperiodic MgO/Si coating on tungsten as a spectrally selective thermal emitter, achieving a modeled 47.0% TPV conversion efficiency with a GaSb cell at 1500 K.
motivation: High thermophotovoltaic efficiencies usually depend on cell-side sub-bandgap photon recycling; the authors instead ask whether emitter-side spectral selectivity can relax those cell requirements.
method: Inverse design / optimization of a 16-layer aperiodic MgO/Si multilayer on a tungsten substrate, evaluated within a detailed-balance framework incorporating polarization- and angle-resolved emissivity, multiple reflections, and Auger nonradiative recombination for a GaSb cell with antireflection coating and Au mirror.
result: At 1500 K the optimized emitter suppresses 97.1% of blackbody-equivalent sub-bandgap power at the source with only 1.0% parasitic absorption in the cell, yielding 47.0% modeled radiative-to-electrical efficiency versus 30.8% for a SiC emitter at comparable maximum power density.
conclusion: Emitter-side spectral engineering can substantially reduce cell-side photon-recycling requirements and deliver significant TPV efficiency gains, offering an alternative design route for thermal-energy conversion.

title: Simulating Space Bounded Read-$k$ PTMs With Space Bounded Read-Once PTMs
authors: Kuan Cheng, Shengtang Huang, Ruiyang Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that read-[MATH] Probabilistic Turing Machines with bounded space [MATH] and running time [MATH] can be simulated by read-once Probabilistic Turing Machines with error [MATH], running in space [MATH] and time [MATH]. As a direct consequence we show that read-[MATH] [MATH] is equal to [MATH], for any constant [MATH]. Recently OpenAI announced that [MATH]. If this is true then our result immediately implies that read-[MATH] [MATH] is equal to [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves that space-bounded read-k Probabilistic Turing Machines can be simulated by read-once PTMs with comparable space and polynomial time overhead, yielding read-k BPL = BPL for constant k.
motivation: Read-k versus read-once randomness access is a natural structural question in space-bounded derandomization and complexity theory, with consequences for classes such as BPL and its read-k variants.
method: Probabilistic Turing machine simulation techniques: transforming a machine that reads each random bit up to k times into a read-once machine, at the cost of an error parameter and polynomial time blow-up while preserving logarithmic space.
result: Read-k PTMs with space s and time t are simulated by read-once PTMs running in space O(s + log t) and polynomial time with small error; consequently read-k BPL equals BPL for every constant k (and matches L under the unproven OpenAI-announced claim BPL = L).
conclusion: Randomness-access restrictions of order k do not enlarge the power of logarithmic-space probabilistic computation, collapsing read-k BPL to BPL.

title: Algebra-Valued Yang-Mills-Type Theories: Polynomial Obstructions And Holonomy Reductions
authors: Willian Goulart Gomes Velasco Yuri Ximenes Lecca
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study algebra-valued Yang-Mills-type ([MATH]-YMT) theories on a smooth [MATH]-manifold [MATH], where connections take values in an [MATH]-graded algebra [MATH] and descend to an associated bundle [MATH]. We derive the field equations, gauge transformations, and generalized Bianchi identities, showing that affine Ehresmann compatibility forces the vertical image of [MATH] into the Lie nucleus [MATH] of [MATH], and that gauge covariance and the Bianchi identity are obstructed precisely by the Jacobiator [MATH] (leaving principal [MATH]-gauge symmetries anomaly-free). We then prove obstructions in three settings. First, internal-product Chern-Weil and self-dual [MATH]-YMT functionals vanish in weak [MATH]-solvable algebras, invariant under [MATH]-splitting extensions. Second, in reductive Cartan-Yang-Mills theories on [MATH], quartic-block parenthesization yields a strict cutoff at [MATH], while binary-tree halving yields an exact Jacobsthal-number cutoff ([MATH], plus rank vanishing for [MATH]). We catalog Berger holonomy reductions for [MATH], proving an on-shell vanishing (torsion-free) vs. off-shell survival (torsionful) dichotomy in 4D for [MATH] and [MATH] connections---via [MATH]---and in 7D for [MATH]-connections. Third, we prove an associator-quotient collapse and Jacobiator vertex dichotomy for odd-dimensional internal [MATH]-Chern-Simons theories, with applications to [MATH]-[MATH] theories, octonionic and reductive Higgs Proca mass spectra, and reductive dualities.
tldr: The paper develops a theory of algebra-valued Yang-Mills-type connections on smooth manifolds graded by an algebra, deriving field equations, gauge transformations and Bianchi identities, and proving several structural obstructions (Chern-Weil/self-dual functional vanishing in weak-solvable algebras, parenthesization cutoff effects, and holonomy reduction dichotomies).
motivation: The authors aim to generalize ordinary Yang-Mills gauge theory to the setting where connections take values in an arbitrary graded algebra descending to an associated bundle, and to understand when gauge covariance, Bianchi identities and characteristic-class functionals fail or survive.
method: They compute field equations, gauge transformations and generalized Bianchi identities for algebra-valued YMT, identify the Jacobiator as the precise obstruction to gauge covariance, and then prove vanishing/cutoff results for Chern-Weil and self-dual functionals, catalog Berger holonomy reductions in 4D and 7D, and analyze associator-quotient collapse in internal Chern-Simons theories.
result: Chern-Weil and self-dual YMT functionals vanish in weak-solvable algebras; quartic-block parenthesization gives a strict cutoff while binary-tree halving yields a Jacobsthal-number cutoff; an on-shell vanishing versus off-shell survival dichotomy is proven for holonomy reductions in 4D and 7D; and an associator-quotient collapse with Jacobiator vertex dichotomy is established for odd-dimensional internal Chern-Simons theories.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic algebraic-geometric obstruction theory for generalized Yang-Mills and Chern-Simons theories, with applications to octonionic and reductive Higgs Proca mass spectra and reductive dualities, though it lies outside quantum information science proper.

title: Resilient Transmission Of Highly Structured Light Via Active Convolved Illumination
authors: Anindya Ghoshroy, James Davis, Martin Wilkens, Sahin K. Ozdemir, Durdu O. Guney
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wave propagation through lossy and noisy systems as well as spatiotemporally dynamic random media often limits the complex information that can be reliably transmitted or retrieved. Progress in adaptive optics, wavefront shaping, machine learning, and wave propagation theories has significantly advanced physical and computational correction techniques. However, many approaches remain constrained by restrictive operating conditions, limiting their ability to meet growing application-specific demands, such as higher spatial resolution in imaging and greater data capacity in communications, particularly in highly dynamic environments. Recently, active convolved illumination (ACI) was proposed as a novel framework for preserving the spatial structure of optical modes during propagation through strongly distorting environments, such as atmospheric turbulence. ACI aims to bypass the prohibitive complexity of global distortion tracking by combining spectrally localized characterization with compensation using a correlated auxiliary source. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of ACI, detailing the formulation of correlation-injecting and auxiliary sources and the role of segmented reciprocal-space characterization and distortion compensation. We explore extensions in free-space optical communication and potential high-precision phase measurement, and numerically evaluate interferometric strategies for experimental implementation. This work highlights ACI as a potentially versatile framework for distortion-resilient light transmission, with broad interdisciplinary utility ranging from atmospheric physics and remote sensing to telecommunications, target tracking, and biomedical diagnosis, offering flexible deployment either as a standalone paradigm or hybridized with existing optical systems.
tldr: This paper reviews active convolved illumination (ACI), an optical wavefront-shaping framework for preserving structured light through lossy, noisy, and dynamic media.
motivation: Reliable transmission and retrieval of complex optical information through turbulent or random media is limited by restrictive operating conditions of existing adaptive-optics and computational correction methods.
method: The authors comprehensively review ACI, including correlation-injecting auxiliary sources, segmented reciprocal-space characterization, and distortion compensation, and numerically evaluate interferometric implementation strategies.
result: The review details ACI's formulation and explores extensions to free-space optical communication and high-precision phase measurement, highlighting its potential as a versatile distortion-resilient light-transmission framework.
conclusion: ACI may offer broad interdisciplinary utility in atmospheric physics, remote sensing, telecommunications, tracking, and biomedical diagnosis, either standalone or hybridized with existing optical systems.

title: The Non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ Affine Laumon Function And Its Difference Equation
authors: Rinat Kedem Philippe Di Francesco
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an explicit [MATH]-Givental type formula for the [MATH] non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions. J. of Int. Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator [MATH], which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine [MATH] Q-system.
tldr: The paper constructs an explicit Givental-type formula for the non-stationary affine gl_N relativistic Toda (affine Laumon) function and proves Shiraishi's conjecture that it satisfies a non-stationary difference equation defined by a quiver automorphism of the affine quantum cluster algebra.
motivation: Shiraishi introduced non-stationary affine Laumon/Ruijsenaars functions and conjectured that they obey a difference equation tied to the quantum cluster algebra of the affine Q-system; this conjecture had remained unproven.
method: The authors derive an explicit Givental-type integral/series representation of the affine Laumon function and analyze the action of an operator realizing a Dehn twist (quiver automorphism) of the affine quantum cluster algebra on this representation.
result: They prove Shiraishi's conjecture, establishing that the non-stationary affine Laumon function satisfies the proposed non-stationary difference equation.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous foundation for non-stationary relativistic Toda/Ruijsenaars systems and their cluster-algebraic structure, with implications for integrable systems and representation theory rather than quantum information.

title: Contractions Of Realizations And Differential Invariants Of The Algebra sl(2,C)
authors: M. Nesterenko M. Staryi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we formalize a method for constructing limit transitions between local realizations of Lie algebras based on contractions of the corresponding algebras. In the complex holomorphic category, contractions of faithful realizations of the special linear algebra sl(2, C) to the complex three-dimensional Poincar\'e algebra and the Weyl-Heisenberg algebra are explicitly constructed. For the contraction of a generating realization of the algebra sl(2,C) to the algebra g_{3.4}^{-1}, differential invariants are constructed and a limit system of Newtonian type is found.
tldr: The paper develops a method for constructing limit transitions between local realizations of Lie algebras via algebra contractions, explicitly worked out for sl(2,C) contracting to the complex Poincaré and Weyl-Heisenberg algebras, with differential invariants and a limiting Newtonian-type system derived for one case.
motivation: Contractions of Lie algebras underlie the study of limiting regimes (e.g. non-relativistic or classical limits) of symmetry structures, but a systematic procedure for transporting realizations and their invariants through contractions has been lacking.
method: The authors formalize a construction of limit transitions between local realizations in the complex holomorphic category, then explicitly build contractions of faithful realizations of sl(2,C) onto the three-dimensional complex Poincaré algebra, the Weyl-Heisenberg algebra, and g_{3.4}^{-1}.
result: Explicit contracted realizations are obtained, and for the contraction to g_{3.4}^{-1} the differential invariants are constructed together with a limiting system of Newtonian type.
conclusion: The framework offers a general recipe for generating invariants and limit equations from Lie algebra contractions, illustrated concretely for sl(2,C); it is a pure mathematics contribution with no direct quantum information, thermodynamic, network, or hybrid-platform content.

title: Polarization Lifetime As A Design Axis For Task-Adaptive Photonic Reservoir Computing
authors: Kathy L\"udge Tao Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic time-delayed reservoir computing (TDRC) based on conventional Class B lasers is limited by fragile external cavity mode (ECM) locking dynamics. Here, we show that engineering the polarization lifetime (T[MATH]) with the carrier lifetime ([MATH]) reshapes the topology and stability of TDRC. Comparing four laser classes (Class A, Class B, Class C[MATH], and Class C[MATH]), a finite polarization lifetime acts as an intrinsic dynamic filter, dissolving discrete ECM chaos grids into continuous, phase-tolerant operational basins. Information processing capacity (IPC) decomposition further exposes distinct computational profiles: matched Class C[MATH] achieves the highest nonlinear capacity (16.28) and the highest total capacity (19.29), whereas Class A exhibits the highest linear capacity (4.70). A task-dependent reversal governs hardware design: Class A and Class C[MATH] achieve comparable, and the lowest, NRMSE on short-horizon Mackey--Glass prediction (0.0103 and 0.0105, within one standard deviation), while the time-scale-matched Class C[MATH] dominates the higher-dimensional Lorenz (0.0506) and the experimental Santa Fe (0.4251) tasks. Linear-IPC ranking matches Mackey-Glass accuracy; nonlinear-IPC ranking matches the Lorenz exactly and Santa Fe within the mask-to-mask uncertainty. Under realistic quantum noise, resilience is dictated mainly by [MATH], not T[MATH]: Class A retains the lowest NRMSE (0.47) even at spontaneous emission factor [MATH] = [MATH], whereas the long-carrier Class B degrades (0.98). A residual T[MATH]-mediated benefit of 20[MATH] persists in the slow-carrier Class C[MATH] (0.78 vs. 0.98). Time-scale engineering thus offers a nuanced design paradigm for optical computing, where optimal hardware is set by the task's time-scale hierarchy rather than a universal figure of merit.
tldr: The paper proposes polarization lifetime as a design axis in photonic time-delayed reservoir computing using different laser classes, showing task-dependent performance tradeoffs and noise resilience.
motivation: Conventional Class B laser-based photonic reservoir computing is limited by fragile external cavity mode locking, motivating alternative laser dynamic regimes and design parameters.
method: The authors compare four laser classes (A, B, C1, C2) and analyze information processing capacity decomposition, Mackey-Glass, Lorenz, and Santa Fe tasks, including effects of spontaneous emission noise.
result: Different laser classes optimize different capacities and tasks: Class C1 gives highest nonlinear/total IPC, Class A gives highest linear IPC, and noise resilience depends mainly on carrier lifetime rather than polarization lifetime.
conclusion: Optimal photonic reservoir hardware is task-dependent and should be chosen according to the time-scale hierarchy of the target computation rather than a universal figure of merit.

title: Projection Of Massive And Interacting Conformal Theories To The Future Null Infinity
authors: Beatrice Costeri, Claudio Dappiaggi, Alberto Ferrari
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a four-dimensional, globally hyperbolic and asymptotically flat spacetime, we consider a real, linear, massive scalar field. Within the framework of perturbative algebraic quantum field theory and inspired by the principle of perturbative agreement, we regard the mass term in the underlying Lagrangian as an interaction potential. This allows us to construct the algebra of observables of the massive theory and, using a M{\o}ller map, to represent its elements as formal power series in the squared mass, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Following [DMP06], we use the bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massless theory to project each coefficient to future null infinity [MATH].In four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, we prove convergence of the projected series in the presence of an infrared cut-off and show that the global adiabatic limit exists but is trivial. We circumvent this obstruction by exploiting the time-slice axiom, which allows us to restrict our attention to observables localized in a causally convex neighbourhood containing a Cauchy hypersurface. Removing the cut-off locally yields a non-trivial limit and hence a bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massive theory. We then extend our procedure to a self-interacting real scalar field. We represent interacting observables as formal power series in the coupling constant, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Each coefficient in the domain of the bulk-to-boundary map can thus be projected to future null infinity. As a concrete example, we apply this method to the stress-energy tensor of a massless scalar field with a quartic self-interaction, computing its projection up to first order in perturbation theory.
tldr: Using perturbative algebraic quantum field theory, the authors project massive and self-interacting scalar field observables onto future null infinity via a bulk-to-boundary correspondence inherited from the massless conformally coupled theory.
motivation: Bulk-to-boundary correspondences are well understood for massless conformal fields, but extending them to massive and interacting theories requires handling the mass term as an interaction and dealing with infrared obstructions.
method: The mass term is treated as an interaction potential, and a Møller map represents massive observables as formal power series in m^2 with coefficients in the massless conformally coupled algebra; each coefficient is then projected to future null infinity, with the construction extended to quartic self-interaction.
result: In Minkowski space the projected series converges under an infrared cutoff, but the global adiabatic limit is trivial; restricting to a causally convex neighbourhood of a Cauchy surface via the time-slice axiom yields a non-trivial local limit and a bulk-to-boundary map for massive theory, illustrated by projecting the stress-energy tensor to first order.
conclusion: A rigorous algebraic framework is established for projecting massive and interacting scalar observables to null infinity, circumventing the trivial global adiabatic limit through localization.

title: Distributionally Robust Risk Evaluation With Low-Rank Perturbations
authors: Linglingzhi Zhu, Dongze Wu, Yao Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study distributionally robust risk under perturbations restricted to low-rank matrices whose row and column spaces are shared across observations, focusing on how much worst-case risk this restriction sacrifices and how to compute the restricted worst case. Under moment or Wasserstein budgets, we derive quantitative bounds on the gap between the unrestricted and low-rank worst-case risks, characterize when the gap vanishes, and identify the smallest lossless row and column dimensions. To generate worst-case perturbations, we apply projected gradient ascent to a curvature-corrected concave problem and derive computable risk certificates. We establish global sublinear convergence for the corrected objective and linear convergence to a worst-case distribution when the budget constraint is sufficiently active.
tldr: The paper studies distributionally robust risk evaluation under low-rank perturbations with shared row and column spaces, deriving bounds on the worst-case risk gap and algorithms for computing worst-case distributions.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how restricting distributional perturbations to low-rank matrices affects worst-case risk and to provide computationally tractable certificates under moment or Wasserstein ambiguity sets.
method: They derive quantitative bounds comparing unrestricted and low-rank worst-case risks, characterize when the gap vanishes, identify minimal lossless dimensions, and use projected gradient ascent on a curvature-corrected concave problem.
result: They obtain computable risk certificates, prove global sublinear convergence for the corrected objective, and establish linear convergence to a worst-case distribution when the budget constraint is sufficiently active.
conclusion: Low-rank restrictions can preserve worst-case risk under certain conditions, and the proposed optimization framework provides efficient computation and convergence guarantees for distributionally robust risk evaluation.

title: Quantum Fundamental Groups Of Spaces With Finite-Sheeted Universal Covers
authors: Shuzhou Wang, Zhenhua Wang, Matthew Zediker
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete quantum groups have attracted much interest, but there was a lack of natural examples until Voigt constructed quantum permutations of finite and infinite sets in arXiv:2208.01310. In this paper, we construct the quantum fundamental groups that contain the classical fundamental groups as subgroups. This is a new class of natural examples of discrete quantum groups arising from symmetries of covering spaces in topology. We characterize quantum fundamental groups for a wide class of examples, including [MATH]. We show that these quantum fundamental groups are genuinely quantum for spaces with finite fundamental groups that are either non-abelian or of non prime order.
tldr: The paper constructs quantum fundamental groups from symmetries of covering spaces, yielding new examples of discrete quantum groups.
motivation: Discrete quantum groups lack natural examples beyond Voigt's quantum permutations, so the authors seek new classes arising from topology.
method: They define quantum fundamental groups containing classical fundamental groups and characterize them for spaces with finite-sheeted universal covers.
result: They show these quantum fundamental groups are genuinely quantum for spaces whose finite fundamental groups are non-abelian or of non-prime order.
conclusion: This provides a topological source of discrete quantum groups, but it is purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Convergence Properties Of PF-Exec: Homogeneous Structure, Anchored Closed Form, And Gain Dynamics
authors: Hanzhang Jia, Liheng Zeng, Yiran Li, Yi Gao, Bo Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes a layered mathematical char acterisation of PF-Exec, the algorithm of the companion system paper. Demand-proportional bandwidth allocation yields an exact first-order homogeneous decomposition, from which the equal-load bandwidth target and its feasibility bound follow in closed form. The logarithmic knee view preserves strict load order and shares its global optimum with the Jain fairness index, while the demand-weighted centroid minimises the position potential. The damped softmax association block possesses a fixed point on the product of simplices. The truncated one-dimensional gain iteration admits a complete characterisation, with geomet ric convergence below the critical gain, initial-value-dependent bounded oscillation at it, and a family of bounded two-state cycles above it. A global invariant error ball and an explicit tracking recursion complete the execution guarantee. A numerical audit confirms the structural identities on every measured state and quantifies the local amplification of the coupled association and resource dynamics. Together, the results explain how closed form recovery directions and bounded adaptive gains provide stable execution without requiring a global Euclidean contraction assumption.
tldr: This paper provides a layered mathematical characterization of the PF-Exec algorithm for demand-proportional bandwidth allocation, including closed-form targets, convergence conditions, and gain dynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to establish rigorous convergence and stability guarantees for an adaptive bandwidth allocation algorithm used in networked systems.
method: They employ exact first-order homogeneous decomposition, derive closed-form expressions for equal-load bandwidth and feasibility, analyze a damped softmax association fixed point, and characterize a truncated one-dimensional gain iteration.
result: The gain iteration exhibits geometric convergence below a critical gain, bounded oscillation at the critical gain, and bounded two-state cycles above it; numerical audits confirm structural identities and quantify local amplification.
conclusion: The results explain how closed-form recovery directions and bounded adaptive gains ensure stable execution without requiring a global Euclidean contraction assumption.

title: Noncommutative Rational Positivstellens\"atze With Operator Coefficients
authors: Abhay Jindal, Igor Klep, Jurij Vol\v{c}i\v{c}
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a convex Positivstellensatz for noncommutative rational functions with bounded operator coefficients. A hermitian operator-valued rational function that is positive semidefinite on a matrix convex set described by a linear pencil admits a positivity certificate consisting of rational hermitian squares and a completely positive term involving the defining linear pencil. The certificate comes with an explicit complexity bound independent of the dimension of the coefficient Hilbert space. As a consequence, we solve the operator-valued noncommutative rational analog of Hilbert's 17th problem: every positive semidefinite operator-valued noncommutative rational function is a sum of hermitian squares, and even a single hermitian square when the coefficient Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional. In contrast, the corresponding commutative statement fails for infinite-dimensional operator coefficients.
tldr: The paper proves convex Positivstellensatz and Hilbert 17th problem analogues for noncommutative rational functions with bounded operator coefficients.
motivation: It addresses positivity certificates for operator-valued noncommutative rational functions on matrix convex sets, extending classical real algebraic geometry to the noncommutative operator setting.
method: The authors establish a convex Positivstellensatz using rational hermitian squares and a completely positive term from the defining linear pencil, with complexity bounds independent of the coefficient Hilbert space dimension.
result: Every positive semidefinite operator-valued noncommutative rational function is shown to be a sum of hermitian squares, and a single hermitian square suffices for infinite-dimensional coefficient Hilbert spaces.
conclusion: The work solves the operator-valued noncommutative rational analogue of Hilbert's 17th problem and highlights a contrast with the commutative case for infinite-dimensional coefficients.

title: Correlation Distribution For A Class Of Niho Exponents Via Self-conjugate-reciprocal Polynomials And Kloosterman Sums
authors: Yongbo Xia, Chunlei Li, Xiangyong Zeng, Tor Helleseth
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] for an even [MATH] and let [MATH] with [MATH]. In this paper, the correlation distribution between a binary m-sequence of period [MATH] and its [MATH]-decimation is considered. The cross-correlation function takes seven values [MATH] for [MATH], and we determine their frequencies based on the study of low-degree self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and three mixed Kloosterman sums, which are finally expressed in terms of [MATH] and [MATH], where [MATH] is the Kloomsterman sum on the finite field [MATH] and [MATH] is a primitive element of [MATH].

motivation: Cross-correlation of m-sequences is central to designing sequences with low correlation for classical communication and coding applications, and Niho exponents are a standard tool for obtaining few-valued correlation spectra.
method: The authors analyze low-degree self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and evaluate three mixed Kloosterman sums over finite fields to count the frequencies of each correlation value.
result: The cross-correlation function is shown to take seven distinct values, with their distribution fully characterized and expressed in terms of Kloosterman sums and a primitive element of the finite field.
conclusion: The work provides a complete correlation distribution for this class of Niho exponents, extending the theory of finite-field sequences, but remains within classical sequence design with no quantum information content.

title: Localization For Lipschitz Monotone Quasi-periodic Operators With Power-law Hopping
authors: Hongyi Cao, Yunfeng Shi, Peizhen Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove spectral and dynamical localization for quasi-periodic operators on [MATH] with Lipschitz monotone potentials and power-law hopping. For sufficiently small coupling, localization holds at every allowed phase whenever the hopping decay exponent [MATH] exceeds the Diophantine exponent [MATH]. The proof is based on multiscale analysis with exponentially growing scales. We use homotopy in the coupling constant to select the local eigenvalue branches and Schur complement estimates to control the successive elimination of coordinates.
tldr: The paper proves spectral and dynamical localization for quasi-periodic operators with Lipschitz monotone potentials and power-law hopping via multiscale analysis.
motivation: Localization phenomena in quasi-periodic operators are central in mathematical condensed matter physics, but the specific setting of Lipschitz monotone potentials with power-law hopping requires new techniques beyond standard Anderson localization proofs.
method: The authors use multiscale analysis with exponentially growing scales, homotopy in the coupling constant to select local eigenvalue branches, and Schur complement estimates to control successive coordinate elimination.
result: For sufficiently small coupling, they establish localization at every allowed phase whenever the hopping decay exponent exceeds the Diophantine exponent.
conclusion: The work extends localization theory to a class of quasi-periodic operators with long-range hopping and monotone potentials, providing rigorous spectral and dynamical localization results.

title: The Train Unit Shunting Problem With Service Scheduling And Workforce Assignment: Classical And Quantum Optimization Approaches
authors: Alessia Ciacco, Francesca Guerriero, Eneko Osaba
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient railway rolling stock management requires the coordinated planning of train-unit assignment, shunting movements, track occupation, service operations, and workforce allocation. These interdependent decisions give rise to a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, particularly as the size of the fleet and the planning horizon increase. This paper introduces the Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment, a mixed-integer linear programming formulation that integrates these operational decisions within a unified optimization framework. To improve computational tractability, a preprocessing procedure is developed to reduce the size of the resulting model. The proposed approach is evaluated through computational experiments on instances of increasing size and under different objective-function weight and cost configurations. Classical optimization experiments using Gurobi show that filtering method reduces the number of decision variables and constraints, while its impact on computational time varies across instances. In addition, a constrained quadratic model representation is investigated using D-Wave's hybrid quantum-classical optimization solver.
tldr: The paper formulates an integrated Train Unit Shunting Problem with service scheduling and workforce assignment as a MILP, solves it with Gurobi after preprocessing, and additionally tests a constrained quadratic model on D-Wave's hybrid quantum-classical solver.
motivation: Railway rolling stock management involves tightly coupled decisions (unit assignment, shunting, track occupation, servicing, workforce), which become intractable for large fleets and long planning horizons, motivating a unified optimization framework.
method: A mixed-integer linear programming formulation integrates all operational decisions, a preprocessing/filtering procedure reduces model size, and the problem is also cast as a constrained quadratic model for D-Wave's hybrid solver; experiments sweep instance sizes and cost configurations.
result: Gurobi experiments show the filtering method reduces variables and constraints, though computational time gains vary by instance; the D-Wave hybrid approach is explored as an alternative representation.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a practical logistics optimization pipeline with a quantum-annealing-flavored alternative, but offers no quantum-information-theoretic or thermodynamic contribution.

title: On The Convergence Of The False Nearest Neighbours Algorithm
authors: Adam \'spiewak
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The False Nearest Neighbours (FNN) algorithm is one of the most widely used methods for choosing the embedding dimension, i.e. the number [MATH] of delay coordinates, in the time-delay reconstruction of a dynamical system from an observed scalar time series. We prove rigorous results on the behaviour of this algorithm for long time series. We consider a smooth dynamical system on a compact manifold [MATH] and an invariant probability measure [MATH]. For a typical measurement function and [MATH]-almost every trajectory, we show that the proportion of false nearest neighbours tends to zero (provided that the tolerance threshold is large enough) once [MATH]. On the other hand, for systems with super-polynomial decay of correlations, we prove that this proportion tends to one whenever [MATH] is smaller than the Hausdorff dimension of [MATH]. Consequently, in this case, the FNN algorithm (run for long enough time series) returns an embedding dimension [MATH] satisfying [MATH]. This is below the threshold [MATH] required by the Takens embedding theorem, so the classical Takens embedding theory does not explain why reconstructions and predictions with [MATH] chosen by the FNN algorithm work in practice. The explanation for this case is provided by a recent probabilistic theory of time-delay embeddings. We apply our results to the H\'enon and Lorenz attractors, showing that the FNN algorithm typically returns [MATH] for the H\'enon map (in the chaotic case) and [MATH] for the Lorenz system.
tldr: Rigorous convergence results are proved for the False Nearest Neighbours algorithm used to select the delay-embedding dimension of a scalar time series.
motivation: FNN is a widely used heuristic for choosing embedding dimension, but its asymptotic behaviour for long time series lacked a rigorous justification, particularly in relation to the Takens threshold.
method: For smooth systems on compact manifolds with invariant measures, the authors analyse the proportion of false nearest neighbours as the embedding dimension M grows, using decay-of-correlations assumptions and probabilistic embedding theory.
result: The false-neighbour proportion tends to zero for large M when the tolerance is large enough, but tends to one for M below the Hausdorff dimension in systems with super-polynomial correlation decay, so FNN typically returns M below the Takens threshold (e.g. M=3 for Hénon, M=6 for Lorenz).
conclusion: Classical Takens theory does not explain the empirical success of FNN-selected dimensions; a recent probabilistic theory of time-delay embeddings is needed instead.

title: Characterizing M-estimators Using Canonical Divergences From Information Geometry
authors: Paul Navas
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On Euclidean space, the losses that produce consistent M-estimators of a functional are its strictly consistent scoring functions (Dimitriadis, Fissler and Ziegel, 2024), and Osband's principle characterizes these through identification functions, which define method-of-moments estimators. We extend this characterization to the probability simplex. We define the residual, which on Euclidean space is a subtraction, as the inverse exponential map of an affine connection. It identifies the exponential barycenter of the connection: the arithmetic, normalized geometric and Fr\'echet means for the mixture, exponential and Levi-Civita connections. Its integral along geodesics is the canonical divergence of Ay and Amari (2015). A geometric form of Osband's principle decides which losses each connection admits. For the flat connections every strictly convex generator yields a consistent Bregman loss. For the curved [MATH]-connections, half the squared Fisher-Rao distance is (up to scale) the only consistent loss for the Fr\'echet mean, and for [MATH] no such loss exists and only the method of moments remains. The residual is integrable only at [MATH], sharpening the integrability claim of Ay and Amari. The characterization yields the estimating equations of regression on the simplex and the calibration decomposition of compositional forecasts.
tldr: The paper characterizes M-estimators on the probability simplex using canonical divergences from information geometry, extending Osband's principle via affine connections.
motivation: Consistent M-estimators on Euclidean space are characterized by strictly consistent scoring functions and Osband's principle, but no analogous characterization existed for the probability simplex.
method: The residual is defined as the inverse exponential map of an affine connection, identifying exponential barycenters (arithmetic, normalized geometric, Fréchet means); its geodesic integral yields the canonical divergence of Ay and Amari, and a geometric Osband's principle determines admissible losses per connection.
result: For flat connections every strictly convex generator gives a consistent Bregman loss; for curved α-connections only half the squared Fisher–Rao distance is consistent for the Fréchet mean at α=0, and for α≠0 only method-of-moments remains; the residual is integrable only at α=0.
conclusion: The framework yields estimating equations for simplex regression and a calibration decomposition for compositional forecasts, sharpening earlier integrability claims.

title: Evolutionary-based Transfer Learning For Physical Attack On End-to-End Autoencoder Communications
authors: Ho Viet Duc Luong, Lang Hong Nguyet Anh, Huynh Thi Thanh Binh, Trinh van Chien
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: End-to-end autoencoder communication has emerged as a promising means of achieving efficient data transmission across various domains. Nevertheless, vulnerabilities have recently been revealed in these systems by adversarial attacks, wherein malevolent entities manipulate the transmitted signals to deceive the autoencoder. This paper leverages the applications of evolutionary algorithms to solve a challenging optimization problem of launching physical attacks against end-to-end autoencoder communication. For white-box scenarios, we introduce PAGA (Physical Attack based on Genetic Algorithm), which combines a genetic algorithm with elite population initialization to craft attack signals that degrade autoencoder performance. To gauge the efficacy of these attack signals, we employ a fitness function that assesses their capacity to induce substantial reconstruction errors and misclassification rates. A Multi-Factorial version of PAGA, referred to as PAMFGA, is proposed to deal with practical scenarios where the attackers have limited knowledge about the receiver, also known as a black-box attack. Our experimental results show that the proposed attacks can substantially degrade the reliability of the considered autoencoder communication systems across the evaluated settings. This study also underscores the critical importance of incorporating security considerations into the design and implementation of end-to-end autoencoder communication systems.
tldr: The paper proposes evolutionary-algorithm-based physical adversarial attacks on end-to-end autoencoder communication systems in white-box and black-box settings.
motivation: End-to-end autoencoder communications are vulnerable to adversarial manipulation of transmitted signals, motivating optimized physical attack strategies.
method: It introduces PAGA, a genetic algorithm with elite population initialization for white-box attacks, and PAMFGA, a multi-factorial variant for black-box attacks with limited receiver knowledge.
result: Experiments show the proposed attack signals substantially degrade reliability by inducing reconstruction errors and misclassification in the evaluated autoencoder communication systems.
conclusion: The study highlights the need to incorporate security considerations into the design of end-to-end autoencoder communication systems.

title: Condensing Law Of Security Information
authors: Qi Tan, Tianyu Cui, Qi Li, Ke Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling laws indicate that the generalization error of a large language model (LLM) decreases monotonically with model size once data is sufficient, and the corollary that larger models outperform smaller ones is now widely accepted. We argue that this corollary fails in security: decisions there hinge on anomalous inputs, which are long-tailed (e.g., zero-day attacks) and therefore poorly served by likelihood fitting. Worse still, the capability brought about by scale (e.g., inferring the intended whole from a corrupted part) leads a LLM silently the anomaly before any downstream security head ever sees it. We formalize this as a tradeoff between two quantities: the cognitive capability [MATH] that a model holds about the world distribution, and the security-information retention [MATH] that survives in its intermediate representation. We derive three information-theoretic bounds to connect them: an upper bound on restoration accuracy in terms of [MATH], an upper bound on [MATH] in terms of the restoration error, and a Fano lower bound on security-task error in terms of [MATH]. These theorems approximately imply that usable security information is a product of how much security information survives and how well it can be extracted, indicating that optimal usable security information can be achieved at a certain model size. We state this as the : usable security information is unimodal in model size, so security generalization error is U-shaped and is minimized at a finite [MATH] rather than decreasing without bound. The experiments on various real-world LLMs validate the condensing law, indicating that there is an optimal model size to solve security issues.
tldr: The paper proposes a 'condensing law of security information' arguing that usable security information in LLMs is unimodal in model size, making security generalization error U-shaped with an optimal finite model size.
motivation: Scaling laws suggest larger LLMs are always better, but the authors argue this fails for security tasks where decisions depend on long-tailed anomalous inputs and where scale-driven 'restoration' capability can silently absorb anomalies before downstream security heads detect them.
method: They formalize a tradeoff between cognitive capability and security-information retention in intermediate representations, deriving three information-theoretic bounds (an upper bound on restoration accuracy, an upper bound on retention in terms of restoration error, and a Fano lower bound on security-task error) and validate empirically on several real-world LLMs.
result: The bounds imply usable security information is a product of surviving and extractable security information, and experiments confirm a U-shaped security generalization error minimized at a finite model size rather than decreasing monotonically.
conclusion: There exists an optimal model size for security applications, contradicting the naive 'bigger is better' corollary of scaling laws; the analysis is classical ML security and does not touch quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: On Applications Of Polynomial-Time Group Isomorphism Algorithm
authors: Wenkang Zhang, Zhinan Wang, Jincheng Zhuang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The group isomorphism problem is a fundamental problem in computational group theory and is closely related to many other problems. Recently, Qiao and Zhang proposed a polynomial-time algorithm for finite group isomorphism in the multiplication-table model that computes the coset of all isomorphisms. Based on the algorithm of Qiao and Zhang, we study applications to finite associative ring isomorphism, bilinear map isotopism over finite commutative rings and free three-tensor isomorphism over finite commutative rings. First, we obtain a polynomial-time algorithm that returns the coset of all isomorphisms for finite associative rings. Second, we extend efficient isotopism and isomorphism algorithms for bilinear maps and free three-tensors from fields to general finite commutative rings.
tldr: The paper extends a polynomial-time finite group isomorphism algorithm to finite associative rings, bilinear map isotopism, and free three-tensor isomorphism over finite commutative rings.
motivation: Group isomorphism is a fundamental computational algebra problem, and the authors seek to leverage a recent polynomial-time algorithm to solve related isomorphism and isotopism problems for rings and multilinear structures.
method: Using the Qiao-Zhang polynomial-time group isomorphism algorithm in the multiplication-table model, the authors derive algorithms that compute cosets of all isomorphisms for finite associative rings and generalize efficient isotopism/isomorphism algorithms for bilinear maps and free three-tensors from fields to finite commutative rings.
result: They obtain polynomial-time algorithms for finite associative ring isomorphism returning the full isomorphism coset, and extend efficient isotopism and isomorphism algorithms to bilinear maps and free three-tensors over general finite commutative rings.
conclusion: The work demonstrates broad applicability of the Qiao-Zhang group isomorphism algorithm to classical algebraic isomorphism problems, but it is unrelated to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Forget The Lineage: Forward-Secure, Lineage-Complete Cryptographic Erasure For LLM-Agent Memory
authors: Yulliwas Ameur, Billal Mokhtari, Samia Bouzefrane
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents keep a long-term memory that the model itself writes: summaries, extracted facts and embeddings derived from what users said. Deleting a message is therefore not enough: its derivatives, storage residue and backups survive. We define lineage-complete forward-secure erasure: after a forget request, an adversary that later obtains all storage and the agent's current keys learns nothing about the forgotten input or any memory derived from it. We present LinEra, which encrypts each memory under a key derived from its parents' keys along the derivation graph; source keys come from a puncturable pseudorandom function, so forgetting is a single puncture and every descendant becomes unreadable without being located. A sound lineage rule records as parents everything the writer saw, which confines all influence of a source to its descendants. We prove security and lineage integrity and integrate LinEra with mem0. With real LLMs from two families (1.5B to 7B parameters) writing the memory of LoCoMo conversations, an attacker holding every file and the current keys recovers, on all ten conversations written by the largest model, 70 of 71 forgotten secrets after logical deletion, 67 with per-object or epoch keys, and none with LinEra; the same holds for every writer tested. The price is a larger forgetting radius, which follows a simple law in the writer's fan-in: forgetting 1% of turns erases 73.0% of derived memories with session-level summaries but only 3.8% with four-turn windows, which also answer better; re-deriving restores what is lost.
tldr: LinEra is a cryptographic erasure scheme that encrypts each LLM-agent memory item under keys derived from its parents' puncturable-PRF keys, so a single key puncture renders all descendants unreadable.
motivation: Deleting a user message from an LLM agent's long-term memory does not remove its derivatives (summaries, facts, embeddings, backups), so a forward-secure, lineage-complete notion of erasure is needed to guarantee that forgotten inputs cannot be recovered even from full storage plus current keys.
method: The authors define lineage-complete forward-secure erasure, build memories into a derivation graph keyed by a puncturable pseudorandom function, record a sound parent rule confining a source's influence to its descendants, prove security and lineage integrity, and integrate the scheme with mem0 evaluated on LoCoMo conversations with 1.5B–7B LLMs.
result: Against an attacker holding all files and current keys, baseline logical deletion leaks 70/71 forgotten secrets and per-object/epoch keys leak 67, whereas LinEra leaks none across all tested writers; the cost is a larger forgetting radius (1% of turns erases 73.0% of derived memories with session summaries but only 3.8% with four-turn windows).
conclusion: Cryptographic lineage-aware erasure can provide strong forgetting guarantees for LLM-agent memory at the price of over-deletion, which can be mitigated by re-deriving lost memories.

title: Stochastic Games With Distributional Entropy Objectives
authors: Shankaranarayanan Krishna, Durgam Latha, Dion Reji, Ashutosh Trivedi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce , two-player zero-sum games whose configurations are probability distributions over the states of a finite arena and whose stage reward is Shannon entropy. Over an infinite discounted horizon, MIN seeks to concentrate the distribution, while MAX seeks to disperse it. Because entropy is nonlinear, it matters whether strategic and transition randomness are averaged before entropy is evaluated or sampled first. We formalise three resulting semantics: averaged-distribution, sampled-profile, and sampled-transition. This semantic choice fundamentally changes the game-theoretic structure. Averaged-distribution games need not be determined, even on a four-state deterministic arena, whereas both sampled semantics are determined and admit optimal stationary randomised strategies. We give contractive Bellman characterisations and convergent finite-horizon approximations for the upper and lower averaged values and the two sampled values. Moreover, even the lower value under averaged-distribution semantics dominates the value under either sampled semantics, while the sampled-profile and sampled-transition values are incomparable in general. For fixed rational discount and positive rational promise gap, the averaged-distribution (upper and lower value) gap problems and both sampled gap problems lie in PSPACE; for a single entropy minimiser, the averaged and sampled-profile problems lie in NP. Finally, under all three semantics, entropy optimisation is NP-hard to approximate within a suitable fixed additive constant, already for deterministic one-player games, where pure memoryless strategies are optimal.
tldr: The paper studies two-player zero-sum stochastic games whose stage reward is Shannon entropy over probability distributions, analyzing three semantics and their game-theoretic and computational properties.
motivation: Entropy is nonlinear, so the order of averaging strategic and transition randomness affects the resulting game semantics and value. The authors aim to formalize and compare these semantics for distributional entropy objectives.
method: They define averaged-distribution, sampled-profile, and sampled-transition game semantics, then derive Bellman characterizations, finite-horizon approximations, determinacy results, and complexity bounds.
result: Averaged-distribution games can be undetermined even on a four-state deterministic arena, while sampled semantics are determined and admit optimal stationary randomized strategies. The averaged lower value dominates sampled values, and gap problems lie in PSPACE or NP in special cases, with NP-hardness of approximation.
conclusion: The choice of entropy-evaluation semantics fundamentally changes stochastic-game structure, determinacy, and complexity. The work is purely classical and game-theoretic, with no direct quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid-systems contribution.

title: Toward A Holographic Representation Theory Of The Bosonic De Sitter Discrete Series
authors: Maryam Bajalan, Jean-Pierre Gazeau, Hamed Pejhan

The proposal exploits two complementary realizations of the same unitary irreducible representation (UIR): a bounded-domain realization on an open ball [MATH] modeling the hyperbolic space [MATH], with [MATH], and a covariant spacetime realization on [MATH], with conformal boundaries [MATH], in which the physical UIR is obtained through the corresponding gauge reduction. This leads to two boundary constructions and an explicit compatibility problem, \;}{\longleftrightarrow}\; \partial\simeq^{3} \quad{\simeq}\quad ^{\pm}\simeq^{3} \;}{\longleftrightarrow}\; _{4} \,. The two outer problems seek explicit intertwiners between the bulk and boundary realizations, with their invariant norms, constraints, and physical quotients properly identified. The middle problem asks how to construct and normalize a unitary intertwiner between the two boundary realizations once both have been shown to carry the same UIR. The bounded picture exposes the unitary and harmonic structure of the representation, while the spacetime picture makes its covariant and gauge-theoretic structure manifest, allowing the two constructions to constrain and illuminate one another. tldr: The paper outlines a mathematical program for a holographic representation theory of the bosonic discrete series of the de Sitter group using bulk-boundary unitary irreducible representation intertwiners.
motivation: The authors aim to connect bounded-domain and covariant spacetime realizations of de Sitter group representations as a step toward a holographic representation theory.
method: The proposal compares a bounded-domain realization on a hyperbolic ball with a covariant spacetime realization on de Sitter space, formulating compatibility and intertwining problems between bulk and boundary constructions.
result: It identifies two boundary constructions and an explicit compatibility problem, with the scalar family serving as a guiding prototype; no concrete physical or information-theoretic results are reported.
conclusion: The work is a mathematical-physics program in group representation theory and holography, not directly connected to the user's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems interests.

title: Deep, Label-free, Volumetric Lifetime Microscopy Via Low-noise, Single Pulse Sampling
authors: Jack Tomkiewicz, Federico Presutti, Tade Marozsak, Jia Zhao, Hatoon Baazim, Hernandez Moura-Silva, Eliezer Calo, Sixian You
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIM) provides label-free metabolic contrast, but conventional time-correlated single-photon counting requires thousands of excitation pulses per pixel to avoid pile-up distortion, limiting imaging speed and increasing motion artifacts and photodamage. Here, we develop single-pulse analog sampling that combines sub-photoelectron read noise with a jitter-immune, frequency-domain estimator for accurate lifetime measurement at low photon counts. Single low-flux traces achieve a photon economy of [MATH] at 100--150 detected photons, enabling accurate lifetime estimation from a single excitation pulse in label-free, volumetric samples. In in vivo zebrafish eyes, single-shot acquisition recovered the lifetime content of 20-pulse averaging at one-twentieth the exposure, resolving endogenous lipofuscin heterogeneity. In intact mouse kidney, scattering and reduced photon throughput impaired lifetime contrast; this was mitigated by lightweight denoisers that enabled label-free lifetime imaging to 200 micron depth at one pulse per pixel. These results establish single-shot FLIM as a route to deeper, faster, motion-tolerant, low-photodamage lifetime imaging.
tldr: The paper presents a low-noise single-pulse sampling method for fluorescence lifetime imaging that enables label-free volumetric lifetime microscopy at very low photon counts.
motivation: Conventional FLIM requires many excitation pulses per pixel, which limits speed and increases photodamage and motion artifacts, so faster and lower-exposure lifetime acquisition is needed for biological imaging.
method: The authors combine sub-photoelectron read noise with a jitter-immune frequency-domain lifetime estimator and demonstrate single-pulse acquisition in label-free samples, using lightweight denoisers to mitigate scattering in deep tissue.
result: Single-shot lifetime estimation at 100–150 detected photons recovered the lifetime content of 20-pulse averaging at one-twentieth the exposure, and denoising enabled label-free lifetime imaging to 200 microns depth in intact mouse kidney.
conclusion: Single-shot FLIM provides a route to deeper, faster, motion-tolerant, and low-photodamage lifetime imaging for biomedical applications.

title: Convergence Analysis Of Physics-informed Neural Networks For Subdiffusion
authors: Bangti Jin, Qiqi Rao, Zhi Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks have emerged as mesh-free solvers for partial differential equations, yet their rigorous convergence theory for time-fractional problems remains limited. We present a convergence analysis of PINNs for linear subdiffusion equations and for the associated backward problem of recovering the initial data from terminal observations. To address the nonlocality and weakly singular kernels of fractional derivatives, we introduce a discretization-based PINN framework built on some popular time-stepping schemes satisfying discrete maximal regularity, including backward Euler, BDF2, L1, and fractional CN schemes. This approach avoids the exact evaluation of fractional derivatives at training points while preserving the stability structure needed for convergence analysis. For the forward problem, we prove that, under the natural fractional maximal-regularity condition [MATH], the piecewise linear temporal reconstructions of PINN-loss minimizers converge to the exact solution. This result avoids the higher-order regularity assumptions on the exact solution that are often imposed in existing PINN convergence analyses. We also verify the required discrete maximal regularity and consistency properties for the aforementioned popular time discretizations. We then extend the analysis to the backward subdiffusion problem and establish convergence of the regularized recovery of the initial data from terminal observations, despite its ill-posedness. Numerical experiments for both forward and backward problems support the theoretical results, demonstrate the necessity of regularization, and show that [MATH]-type losses alone are generally insufficient. These results establish a rigorous theoretical basis for discretization-based PINNs for time-fractional diffusion problems.
tldr: A rigorous convergence analysis of discretization-based physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for forward and backward time-fractional subdiffusion equations.
motivation: PINNs are widely used as mesh-free PDE solvers, but their convergence theory for time-fractional problems with nonlocal, weakly singular kernels is largely undeveloped, so a rigorous theoretical basis is needed.
method: The authors introduce a discretization-based PINN framework built on time-stepping schemes (backward Euler, BDF2, L1, fractional Crank–Nicolson) satisfying discrete maximal regularity, avoiding exact evaluation of fractional derivatives at training points while retaining stability structure.
result: Under a natural fractional maximal-regularity condition, piecewise linear temporal reconstructions of PINN-loss minimizers converge to the exact solution for the forward problem, and regularized recovery of initial data converges for the ill-posed backward problem; numerical experiments confirm the theory and the necessity of regularization.
conclusion: The work establishes a rigorous convergence foundation for discretization-based PINNs applied to time-fractional diffusion problems, showing that L2-type losses alone are generally insufficient.

title: Rate Optimal Streaming Codes Under An Extended Delay Profile For Three-Node Relay Networks
authors: Ke Wang, Wenjie Ma, Zhipeng Li, Yaqiang Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study streaming codes for a three-node relay network with burst lengths [MATH] and an end-to-end decoding delay [MATH]. Existing adaptive schemes for equal bursts approach the same rate upper bound asymptotically using time-varying convolutional codes and lie outside the non-adaptive setting considered here.

result: They characterize rate optimality conditions, including an iff condition for equal burst lengths and a quantitative upper bound showing a strictly positive rate gap in every nondivisible case.
conclusion: The work provides rate-optimal streaming code constructions and converses for relay networks, but it is a classical coding/network information theory contribution with no direct quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networking, or hybrid quantum systems relevance.

title: Causal And Conditional Tail Coefficients: Asymptotics, Inference And Graph Recovery
authors: Mario Krali Axel B\"ucher
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The causal tail coefficient (CTC) measures the influence of an extreme value of one variable on another variable and has been proposed as a tool for causal discovery in heavy-tailed models. Despite its popularity, the asymptotic behavior of its empirical counterpart has not been well understood. We develop an asymptotic theory for the rank-based CTC estimator with an intermediate threshold under nonparametric conditions that are satisfied by all standard copula models. A key observation is that the CTC is determined by the mean of a conditional tail limit distribution, which clarifies its interpretation and determines the asymptotic variance of the estimator. We establish joint asymptotic normality for the entire CTC matrix and prove consistency of a multiplier bootstrap for simultaneous inference. For heavy-tailed linear and recursive max-linear structural equation models, we show that the CTC equals one if and only if the first variable is an ancestor of the second, which leads to confidence graphs for the ancestral graph with asymptotic coverage guarantees. All results extend to general conditional tail coefficients, defined as further functionals of the conditional tail limit distribution. A simulation study and an application to dietary intake data illustrate the methods.
tldr: The paper develops asymptotic theory, inference, and graph-recovery methods for causal tail coefficients in heavy-tailed causal models.
motivation: The causal tail coefficient is used for causal discovery in heavy-tailed settings, but its empirical estimator lacked a rigorous asymptotic understanding.
method: The authors establish joint asymptotic normality for rank-based CTC estimators under nonparametric copula conditions, prove multiplier-bootstrap consistency, and derive graph-recovery guarantees for heavy-tailed linear and recursive max-linear SEMs.
result: The CTC is characterized via the mean of a conditional tail limit distribution, enabling simultaneous inference and confidence graphs for ancestral relations.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides valid asymptotic inference and graph recovery for causal tail coefficients, illustrated by simulations and dietary intake data.

title: RuralShield: Super Intelligence-Assisted Security Triage And Serverless Infrastructure For Resource-Constrained Healthcare
authors: Asif Ahmed Mohammad Arman Ullah
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resource-constrained healthcare providers must connect cloud security controls to an operational response process. Introducing language-model assessments adds an authorization problem: a recommendation must be converted into a permitted action against a specific resource. RuralShield combines a configurable serverless application foundation with structured model assessment, deterministic routing, and human-approved containment. Its design separates workload access, assessment validation, and action authorization so that each boundary produces inspectable records. We evaluate the implementation through a frozen 120-hour non-AI workload and separate desktop and AWS AI cohorts. The workload recorded 999,861 authenticated requests and 999,860 successful responses, with one HTTP 404 and one missing minute representing 139 scheduled requests. Median, 95th-percentile, and 99th-percentile Ohio client latencies were 28.57, 53.01, and 110.77 ms. Eight successful model requests exercised assessment and reporting in two four-case cohorts. The AWS cohort and five scripted controls produced nine completed workflows, including two human-approved Lambda containment cases with verified restoration of the original concurrency setting. Source-linked, checksum-verified archives preserved the records before scoped cleanup. The study demonstrates an inspectable integration of application controls and human-mediated AI response under the evaluated synthetic conditions.
tldr: RuralShield is a serverless cloud-security triage system for resource-constrained rural healthcare providers that uses structured LLM assessments with deterministic routing and human-approved containment actions.
motivation: Rural healthcare providers need to translate cloud security recommendations into auditable, authorized operational responses, and introducing language-model assessments creates an authorization gap between recommendation and permitted action.
method: The system combines a configurable serverless application foundation with structured model assessment, deterministic routing, and human-approved containment, separating workload access, assessment validation, and action authorization so each boundary yields inspectable records; it is evaluated with a 120-hour frozen non-AI workload plus desktop and AWS AI cohorts.
result: The workload recorded 999,861 authenticated requests with 99.9998% success, median/95th/99th-percentile client latencies of 28.57/53.01/110.77 ms, and nine completed workflows including two human-approved Lambda containment cases with verified restoration of concurrency settings.
conclusion: The study demonstrates an inspectable integration of application controls and human-mediated AI response under synthetic conditions, but it addresses applied cloud security engineering rather than quantum information science.

title: Game-Theoretic Analysis Of RIS-Assisted Challenge-Response Pla - Part Ii: Partial Channel Knowledge
authors: Anna V. Guglielmi, Linda Senigagliesi, Marco Baldi, Stefano Tomasin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a physical layer authentication scenario in which a legitimate user (Alice) communicates with an authenticator (Bob) through a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), controlled by Bob. An attacker (Trudy) aims to impersonate Alice by suitably precoding her messages and still transmitting them through the RIS. This two-part study analyzes this attack-defense interaction between Bob and Trudy under perfect (Part I) and partial (Part II) channel knowledge by all the agents. Part I formulates the joint RIS selection and precoder design under perfect channel knowledge as a finite zero-sum game, establishing exact channel subspace conditions for attack indistinguishability alongside equilibrium mixed strategies. Part II extends the defense to incomplete channel information, where each agent observes only its own channel, by formulating a finite-action Bayesian game and characterizing the resulting Bayesian Nash equilibrium.
