Within this framework, we introduce nonhydrostatic columnar models with polynomial vertical buoyancy structure, extending the hydrostatic stratified hierarchy. Retaining the temporal endpoint pairing, we construct transported relabeling generators and evaluate their vorticity-dependent conserved integrals, assuming that spatial boundary terms vanish. For stratified columnar models, preservation of the effective buoyancy entering the Lagrangian suffices for symmetry even when individual buoyancy coefficients change, yielding conserved quantities that generally are not Casimirs of the full Lie--Poisson bracket. Where the Legendre transform is regular, we state the corresponding brackets and identify their Casimir families. The hydrostatic parent is treated directly through the Euler--Poincar\'e principle because its Legendre transform is degenerate. Integrals following directly from advection are distinguished from those obtained through the Noether pairing.
tldr: The paper derives conserved integrals of hydrostatic and nonhydrostatic reduced-gravity upper-ocean models as Noether quantities tied to particle relabeling symmetry, unified in an Euler–Poincaré framework.
motivation: Upper-ocean models (both hydrostatic and nonhydrostatic, vertically unrestricted and columnar) lack an explicit account of which conserved quantities arise from relabeling symmetry versus pure advection, and how columnar reduction interacts with the underlying Lie-algebra structure.
method: Uses the Euler–Poincaré variational principle in Lagrangian (relabeling) form, introducing transported relabeling generators with temporal endpoint pairing and evaluating vorticity-dependent conserved integrals under vanishing spatial boundary terms; new nonhydrostatic columnar models with polynomial vertical buoyancy structure are constructed, and Legendre transforms, brackets, and Casimir families are identified where regular.
result: Conserved integrals follow either directly from advection or from the Noether pairing; for stratified columnar models preservation of the effective buoyancy suffices for symmetry even when individual buoyancy coefficients vary, and the resulting quantities are generally not Casimirs of the full Lie–Poisson bracket. The hydrostatic parent is handled directly via the Euler–Poincaré principle owing to its degenerate Legendre transform.
conclusion: Columnar velocity reduction preserves the Lie-algebra structure, giving a common Euler–Poincaré framework for hydrostatic and nonhydrostatic upper-ocean models and yielding a systematic classification of relabeling-symmetry conservation laws.

title: Spatial Scaling Of Heterogeneity Transfer From Boron Concentration To Absorbed Dose In Boron Neutron Capture Therapy
authors: Roni Muslim, Bidhari Pidhatika, Sutanto Sutanto, Ramacos Fardela, Rio Natanel Wijaya
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how the amplitude and spatial correlation length of boron-concentration fluctuations affect the boron-induced absorbed-dose distribution in boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT). The spatial energy-deposition response of alpha particles and lithium nuclei is obtained using Geant4 and convolved with three-dimensional correlated lognormal boron fields under a uniform neutron field. Approximately [MATH] of the reaction-product energy is deposited within a radius of [MATH], with a characteristic deposition length of [MATH]. Dose heterogeneity increases with both the fluctuation amplitude [MATH] and correlation length [MATH], while the transfer factor [MATH] exhibits an approximate scaling collapse as a function of [MATH]. Analytical Gaussian and lognormal--Gaussian models provide reference predictions for this behavior. At short correlation lengths, the Geant4 response yields a higher transfer factor than a Gaussian response with the same characteristic length, highlighting the influence of the energy-deposition shape on dose smoothing. For [MATH], defined as the dose received by at least [MATH] of the modeled volume, the relative difference between homogeneous and heterogeneous boron-dose models reaches [MATH] at [MATH] and a target ratio [MATH]. We show that mean boron concentration alone is insufficient to characterize spatial nonuniformity of the boron-dose component.
tldr: This study models how spatial fluctuations in boron concentration affect absorbed-dose heterogeneity in boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT).
motivation: BNCT dose planning typically relies on mean boron concentration, but spatial nonuniformity may significantly alter the deposited dose and treatment metrics.
method: The authors use Geant4 to obtain the spatial energy-deposition response of alpha particles and lithium nuclei, then convolve it with three-dimensional correlated lognormal boron fields under a uniform neutron field.
result: Dose heterogeneity increases with fluctuation amplitude and correlation length, and the transfer factor shows an approximate scaling collapse; for D90 the relative difference between homogeneous and heterogeneous models can be substantial.
conclusion: Mean boron concentration alone is insufficient to characterize spatial nonuniformity of the boron-dose component in BNCT.

title: A Necessary And Sufficient Condition For Complete Te/tm Separability In Fully Anisotropic Waveguides
authors: Jie Liu Wei Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A necessary and sufficient condition is established for complete transverse-electric/transverse-magnetic (TE/TM) separability in waveguides homogeneously filled with a fully anisotropic and lossless medium. The permittivity and permeability tensors are Hermitian positive-definite and may contain nonzero transverse--longitudinal coupling terms. Complete TE/TM separation occurs if and only if the transverse permeability block is proportional to the transpose of the transverse permittivity block and the corresponding transverse--longitudinal coupling vectors satisfy the same proportionality relation after complex conjugation. The longitudinal constitutive entries remain independent apart from positive definiteness. The condition is derived directly from the source-free Maxwell equations, and independent analyses of the TE and TM modes lead to the same material relation. Since no boundary condition enters the derivation, the criterion is independent of the boundary type. Full-vector waveguide mode analyses using our in-house programs for perfect-electric-conductor and Bloch-periodic waveguides, with material tensors satisfying and violating the condition, agree with the theoretical results.
tldr: The paper derives a necessary and sufficient material-tensor condition for complete TE/TM mode separability in waveguides filled with fully anisotropic lossless media.
motivation: TE/TM mode separation is useful for simplifying waveguide analysis, but in fully anisotropic media with transverse-longitudinal coupling the conditions under which complete separation is possible are not fully characterized.
method: The condition is derived directly from source-free Maxwell equations by independently analyzing TE and TM modes, and is tested with full-vector mode simulations for perfect-electric-conductor and Bloch-periodic waveguides.
result: Complete TE/TM separability holds if and only if the transverse permeability block is proportional to the transpose of the transverse permittivity block and the transverse-longitudinal coupling vectors satisfy the same proportionality after complex conjugation.
conclusion: The criterion is boundary-condition independent and provides a practical material-design rule for achieving complete TE/TM separation in anisotropic waveguides.

title: Composition Operators On Weighted Beurling--Sobolev Spaces
authors: Rachid Zarouf St\'ephane Charpentier (I2M)
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a function [MATH] holomorphic in a neighborhood of the closed unit disk [MATH], we study the matrix \[ A_\varphi = \big((k)\big)_{n,k\geq 0}. \] We obtain a complete characterization of those [MATH] for which [MATH] acts boundedly from [MATH] to [MATH], [MATH]. These results can be reformulated in terms of composition operators, providing a complete description of the symbols [MATH] holomorphic in a neighbourhood of [MATH] that induce a bounded composition operator [MATH] between two possibly different Beurling--Sobolev spaces. In particular, we prove that [MATH] is bounded on [MATH] for some [MATH] if and only if it is bounded on every [MATH], [MATH], if and only if [MATH] satisfies an analytic condition at the points of [MATH] where it touches the unit circle. Extensions to weighted Beurling--Sobolev spaces are also provided.
tldr: This paper characterizes bounded composition operators on weighted Beurling--Sobolev spaces via an associated matrix and analytic conditions on the symbol near the unit circle.
motivation: The work addresses a pure complex-analysis/operator-theory question about composition operators between Beurling--Sobolev spaces.
method: The authors study a matrix associated with a holomorphic symbol and derive boundedness criteria, reformulating the results in terms of composition operators.
result: They obtain a complete characterization of symbols inducing bounded composition operators between possibly different Beurling--Sobolev spaces, including an analytic condition at boundary contact points, with extensions to weighted spaces.
conclusion: The paper provides a full operator-theoretic classification, but it has no apparent connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Cut Finite Element Method With Boundary Value Correction For Robin, Neumann And Interface Conditions
authors: Erik Burman, Peter Hansbo, Mats G. Larson
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the cut finite element method with boundary value correction of Burman, Hansbo and Larson [Math.\ Comp.\ 87 (2018) 633--657] to Robin and Neumann conditions and to interface problems with imperfect bonding. The formulation retains a piecewise affine boundary for all integration, while using the exact geometry only at boundary quadrature points. The correction uses Taylor expansions of the solution and its gradient along the discrete normal, with the exact normal used to evaluate the transported flux. At an interface, a further correction to the normal flux jump accounts for the difference between these two normals. Under the stated trace and Poincar\'e bounds, the corrected form is an [MATH] perturbation of a symmetric form, whose matrix can therefore be used as a preconditioner. For a fixed finite Robin coefficient, we obtain the energy error bound [MATH], whereas the bound uniform in the Robin coefficient is [MATH], provided the Poincar\'e constant is uniform. With [MATH], the sufficient Taylor orders are therefore [MATH] and [MATH], respectively. Numerical examples for [MATH] illustrate these rates and the effect of the flux-jump correction in the interface problem.
tldr: The paper extends a cut finite element method with boundary value correction to Robin, Neumann, and imperfect-bonding interface conditions, deriving energy error bounds in terms of Taylor correction orders.
motivation: Cut finite element methods use a simple background mesh with a piecewise affine approximation of the boundary, which introduces geometric error; prior work handled Dirichlet conditions, and this work aims to cover Robin, Neumann, and interface problems.
method: Taylor expansions of the solution and its gradient along the discrete normal are used to correct boundary values, with exact normals at quadrature points for transported flux and an additional correction of the normal flux jump at interfaces; the corrected form is a compact perturbation of a symmetric form usable as a preconditioner.
result: For fixed Robin coefficient the energy error bound is of order h^{k+1/2}, while a bound uniform in the Robin coefficient requires uniform Poincare constant, giving sufficient Taylor orders p >= k+1 and p >= k+2 respectively; numerical examples confirm the rates.
conclusion: Boundary value correction is shown to be viable for Robin, Neumann, and interface conditions in cut finite element methods, with rigorous error estimates and demonstrated convergence.

title: First-order Characterizations Of Strong Quasiconvexity With The Exact Modulus
authors: John Matos Ascona, Jackeline C. Huaccha Neyra, Lizet Santa Cruz Calder\'on, Heraclio L\'opez-L\'azaro
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study first-order characterizations of strong quasiconvexity for functions defined on convex subsets of real normed spaces. For functions that are continuous along segments, an inequality involving the lower Dini derivative is a known necessary condition for strong quasiconvexity with a given modulus, whereas the established converse guarantees only half of that modulus. By means of a one-dimensional lemma, we prove that this inequality, and even its weaker version with the upper Dini derivative, ensures strong quasiconvexity with the same modulus, without requiring the domain to be open; this answers a question raised in the recent literature. The main result leads to a characterization with the same modulus in terms of the Clarke subdifferential for locally Lipschitz functions on Banach spaces, which answers another open question, and to a formula for the exact modulus of radial functions defined on Hilbert spaces. We also present some consequences in optimization, such as an optimality condition without Clarke regularity, an error bound with optimal constant and, for the projected subgradient method, the same convergence rate as in the strongly convex case, together with the exponential convergence of the associated flow. Finally, we show that the converse of a relation between proximal points and strong subdifferentials fails in general, but holds for a truncation of the function.
tldr: The paper gives first-order characterizations of strongly quasiconvex functions on convex subsets of normed spaces using Dini derivatives and Clarke subdifferentials, with the exact modulus.
motivation: Prior work established only a necessary condition for strong quasiconvexity via a lower Dini derivative inequality, and the converse recovered merely half of the modulus; the authors close this gap and settle several open questions in the optimization literature.
method: A one-dimensional lemma is used to show that the Dini-derivative inequality (even in its weaker upper-derivative form) suffices for strong quasiconvexity with the same modulus on non-open domains; this is extended to Clarke subdifferential characterizations for locally Lipschitz functions on Banach spaces.
result: The authors obtain exact-modulus characterizations, a formula for the exact modulus of radial functions on Hilbert spaces, an optimality condition without Clarke regularity, an error bound with optimal constant, the strongly-convex convergence rate for projected subgradient, and exponential convergence of the associated flow.
conclusion: The results resolve open questions on strong quasiconvexity and yield sharper tools for nonsmooth optimization, though they lie entirely within classical convex analysis and optimization.

title: High-Dimensional Gaussian And Bootstrap Approximation: Near $1/\sqrt{n}$ Rates With General Covariance
authors: Ricardo Masini Miles E. Lopes
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider Berry-Esseen bounds over rectangles for sums of [MATH] random vectors in [MATH] that are i.i.d. A longstanding open question in high-dimensional probability and statistics is whether bounds of order [MATH] are attainable up to factors of [MATH] when the population covariance matrix is unrestricted. We answer this question affirmatively, provided that the random vectors have sub-Gaussian entries with non-zero variance. In addition, we provide analogous results for bootstrap approximation and Gaussian comparison, which make use of a special discrepancy measure between covariance matrices that enables improvement with respect to prior work. Taking an approach based on interpolation, the novel aspects of the proofs deal with bounding the interpolation derivatives in a way that is not sensitive to the covariance structure.
tldr: The paper establishes near-1/sqrt(n) Berry-Esseen bounds over rectangles for sums of high-dimensional i.i.d. sub-Gaussian random vectors with unrestricted covariance, together with analogous bootstrap and Gaussian comparison results.
motivation: Whether optimal-order Gaussian approximation rates are attainable in high dimensions without covariance restrictions was a longstanding open question in high-dimensional probability and statistics.
method: The authors use an interpolation-based argument, bounding interpolation derivatives in a way insensitive to the covariance structure, and introduce a discrepancy measure between covariance matrices to sharpen comparisons.
result: They obtain Berry-Esseen-type bounds of order near 1/sqrt(n) up to logarithmic factors under sub-Gaussian entries with non-zero variance, plus matching bootstrap approximation and Gaussian comparison guarantees.
conclusion: The work resolves the open problem affirmatively and provides improved covariance-sensitive tools, but it lies entirely in classical high-dimensional statistics with no quantum information, thermodynamic, network, or hybrid-platform content.

title: A Narrow Band Method For Non-causal Discretizations Of Anisotropic Eikonal Equations, With Adaptive Width, Sub-and Super-solution Construction, And Quasi-linear Complexity
authors: Jean-Marie Mirebeau (CNRS, CB), Yanis Mouheb
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe a narrow band method for numerically solving anisotropic eikonal equations, and more generally static first order Hamilton-Jacobi equations with possibly non-convex Hamiltonians, discretized using standard schemes (semi-Lagrangian, upwind-differences, Lax-Friedrichs). The causality property is not needed, in contrast with the fast marching method. The proposed approach simultaneously builds a numerical sub-solution u and super-solution u to the problem, and adapts the width of the narrow band based on their comparison. We prove that (1 + [MATH])u [MATH] u at termination, where [MATH] > 0 is any given tolerance parameter, and that the worst case complexity is O(N | ln [MATH]| ln(N/[MATH])), where N denotes the number of discretization points, and the underlying constant is explicit in terms of those associated with the scheme properties. Numerical experiments illustrate our results.
tldr: The authors introduce a narrow band numerical method for anisotropic eikonal and static first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations that does not require causality, using simultaneous sub- and super-solution construction with adaptive band width.
motivation: Fast marching-type solvers rely on a causality property that fails for anisotropic or non-convex Hamiltonians, so a more general label-setting-style algorithm with guaranteed error control and near-linear complexity is needed.
method: The scheme alternately builds a numerical sub-solution and super-solution on a discretization (semi-Lagrangian, upwind differences, Lax-Friedrichs) and adaptively sets the narrow band width by comparing them, with a proof that (1+eps)u <= u_bar at termination.
result: Worst-case complexity is O(N |ln eps| ln(N/eps)) with explicit constants depending on scheme properties, and numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical guarantees.
conclusion: The method provides a certified, causality-free solver for anisotropic eikonal problems with quasi-linear scaling, extending fast-marching ideas to non-causal discretizations.

title: An Entropy-stable Splitting Strategy For A Hyperbolic Dispersive Shallow-water Model On Unstructured Meshes
authors: Fr\'ed\'eric Couderc, Arnaud Duran, Maria Kazakova, Bastien Lombard, Pascal Noble, R\'emy Baraille, Jean-Paul Vila
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an entropy-stable splitting strategy for the numerical solution of a hyperbolic approximation of the Serre--Green--Naghdi (SGN) model, leading to an efficient solver for dispersive water waves on unstructured meshes. The model was introduced by Escalante et al. (2019) and justified shortly thereafter by Richard (2021) as an asymptotic model of the free-surface Euler equations under a weak compressibility assumption. While the parent model includes full topography terms and enhanced dispersive properties, the present study focuses on its mild-slope form without enhanced dispersion, which retains an exact energy equation, the cornerstone of the stability analysis. The splitting yields a shallow-water subsystem with two passive scalars, governed by the gravity waves, and an acoustic subsystem carrying the dispersive effects, governed by the acoustic waves. The gravity step adapts an existing entropy-stable scheme, while an original scheme is derived for the acoustic step; both dissipate the energy at the discrete level, under local fully discrete stability criteria on general unstructured meshes. Complementary linear analyses select the low-dissipation calibration of the gravity step used in the computations, outside the scope of the nonlinear estimate. The acoustic step, which requires no global linear solve, is sub-iterated after each gravity time step; the resulting solver is three to six times more expensive than a classical shallow-water solver, depending on the chosen acoustic speed. Numerical validations, ranging from academic benchmarks to a realistic coastal configuration, highlight the properties of the approach and pave the way for operational use.
tldr: The paper develops an entropy-stable operator-splitting numerical scheme for a hyperbolic approximation of the Serre-Green-Naghdi dispersive shallow-water model on unstructured meshes.
motivation: Dispersive shallow-water models such as the SGN system are expensive to solve numerically, and robust, provably stable discretizations on unstructured meshes are needed for coastal and operational ocean modelling.
method: The equations are split into a shallow-water gravity subsystem with two passive scalars and an acoustic subsystem carrying dispersion; each step uses an entropy-stable finite-volume scheme (an existing one adapted for gravity, a new one derived for the acoustic step) with local fully discrete stability criteria, plus linear analyses to calibrate dissipation.
result: Both steps dissipate a discrete energy under the derived local criteria on general unstructured meshes, and numerical tests from academic benchmarks to a realistic coastal configuration confirm stability and accuracy, at a cost three to six times that of a classical shallow-water solver.
conclusion: The splitting strategy yields a provably entropy-stable and efficient solver for dispersive water waves, paving the way toward operational use; it lies outside quantum information science.

title: Safety Certificates For Systems Under Attack Via Stackelberg Set Games
authors: Nikolaos Athanasopoulos, David Laverty, Gregory Provan, Quanyan Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a Stackelberg set selection game for linear systems subject to bounded disturbances and additive attacks. The defender selects the vector parameter of a polytopic safe set template; the attacker, after observing this choice, selects the vector parameter of an admissible attack set. The payoff is a signed, facet-normalised invariance margin that tests invariance exactly and quantifies either the available contraction or the facet inflation needed when invariance fails. Both controlled and robust controlled invariance are treated, corresponding to different information patterns for the control input. Exploiting the structure of parameterised polyhedra, we show that within each validity region the margin is concave in the attack parameter, which reduces the follower minimisation to finitely many extreme parameters. The complete max--min game is then solved by a finite family of LPs, one per defender validity region, each enforcing all attacker regions under a common defender decision and guaranteed margin. The framework handles hard state constraints and additional costs related to the safe set size, and recovers optimal set parameters together with state and attack realisations that activate the certificate. A load frequency control example under false data injection illustrates the construction, the validity decomposition, and the two information patterns.
tldr: The paper formulates a Stackelberg game for selecting safe sets in attacked linear systems and solves it via finite linear programs.
motivation: It aims to certify safety for control systems under bounded disturbances and additive attacks by jointly optimizing defender safe-set parameters and anticipating attacker set choices.
method: The authors use a facet-normalized invariance margin, exploit concavity in attack parameters within validity regions, and reduce the max-min game to a finite family of linear programs.
result: The framework computes optimal set parameters and attack/state realizations, and is illustrated on a load frequency control example under false data injection.
conclusion: The work provides a tractable certificate framework for robust controlled invariance in adversarial control settings, but it is unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Active Learning Of Temporal Specifications Through Distinguishing Queries
authors: Xiaowei Huang Rajarshi Roy
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temporal specifications are essential for verification and monitoring, yet writing formulas that capture the intended behaviour is difficult. Active learning derives such specifications through interaction between a learner and a teacher, but remains underexplored for temporal logics. Existing approaches require the teacher to answer equivalence queries and to construct counterexamples, and they often rely on SAT-based learning procedures that restart the search after each new example. We present an active-learning framework for LTLf in which the teacher only labels traces and answers natural-language questions about the intended behaviour. The learner maintains an enumerated version space of candidate formulas, generates traces that distinguish candidates, and uses the teacher's hints to rank candidates or to restrict the search. We prove consistency with the observed examples, identification within bounded hypothesis classes with a bound on the number of queries, and a PAC guarantee for the final hypothesis. In experiments with a simulated teacher on 36 targets, including targets in four standard environments, the learner identifies every target when it compares all rivals, with fewer than seven queries beyond an initial sample of ten traces on average. Correct hints reduce the number of queries by up to 16% and the number of generated candidates by a fifth, and hints used for ranking never prevent identification, even when incorrect. Our enumeration-based version space is faster than the SAT-based approach of previous learners at every target size.
tldr: An active-learning framework learns LTLf temporal specifications from trace labels and natural-language hints, with consistency, identification, and PAC guarantees.
motivation: Writing temporal-logic specifications is hard, and existing active-learning approaches burden teachers with equivalence queries, counterexample construction, and SAT-based learners that restart after each new example.
method: The learner maintains an enumerated version space of candidate LTLf formulas, generates distinguishing traces as queries, and uses teacher hints to rank or restrict candidates; theory covers consistency, bounded identification, and PAC guarantees.
result: On 36 simulated targets the learner identified every target while comparing all rivals, needing fewer than seven queries beyond ten initial traces on average; correct hints cut queries by up to 16% and candidate generation by about a fifth, and incorrect ranking hints did not prevent identification.
conclusion: Enumeration-based version-space learning outperforms prior SAT-based learners at every target size, showing promise for interactive specification mining in formal verification.

title: From Bytes To Behavior: Request-Level Attribution From Live Gpu Hidden States
authors: Jonathan Pan, Yidi Yuan, Xin Wei Chia, Xinhui Su, Vincent Tan, Brenda Ong
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing memory forensics for machine learning systems typically targets static artifacts, such as model weights or prompt logs, rather than the transient computational states of a live inference process. This gap limits an examiner's ability to analyze the specific behavior of a running large language model (LLM) service that cannot be restarted or modified. We present a method for acquiring per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU process using a non-modifying debugger, without requiring prior knowledge of the model's architecture parameters or weights. The approach employs a general six-stage process with platform-specific adapters, utilizing either a PyTorch allocator clock or a kernel-launch clock to identify and read tensor allocations from video memory. We validate this acquisition on 33 open-source decoder-only models across nine architecture classes, demonstrating that the recovered bytes are byte-exact and usable for downstream analysis. As a use case, we apply linear probes trained on standard framework activations to the recovered states, successfully distinguishing refusal from compliance with an AUROC of 0.88 on held-out prompts. This work establishes that live, observational access to intermediate hidden states is feasible on named inference platforms, providing a new source of evidence for examining the operational behavior of deployed AI systems.
tldr: The paper presents a debugger-based method to extract per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU running an LLM, and uses them for behavioral attribution such as distinguishing refusal from compliance.
motivation: Existing memory forensics for ML systems targets static artifacts like weights or prompt logs, leaving a gap for analyzing the transient internal states of a running model that cannot be restarted or modified.
method: A non-modifying debugger reads tensor allocations from video memory via a six-stage process with platform adapters, using a PyTorch allocator clock or a kernel-launch clock, validated on 33 open-source decoder-only models across nine architecture classes.
result: Recovered activation bytes are byte-exact, and linear probes trained on framework activations distinguish refusal from compliance on the recovered hidden states with AUROC 0.88 on held-out prompts.
conclusion: Live observational access to intermediate hidden states is feasible on deployed inference platforms, offering a new forensic evidence source for examining operational behavior of AI systems.

title: Fair And Efficient Distributed Ev Charging Coordination Using Threshold Cryptography And Machine Learning
authors: Md. Mainul Islam, Muhammad Ismail, Hasan Kurban, Abdulrahman Takiddin, Erchin Serpedin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17577v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Distributed coordination of electric vehicle (EV) charging with the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) keeps EV constraints private but assumes that every participant follows the algorithm. This assumption fails in practice, where a biased operator or a man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacker can send inconsistent signals to different EVs, and compromised EVs can deviate from their prescribed updates. We first prove that attacks by such arbitrarily malicious, i.e., Byzantine, participants do not prevent convergence and therefore remain undetected, and derive the most damaging attack in closed form. We then propose a framework that combines a threshold-signed broadcast with upload recomputation, which detects every deviation without false alarms at linear instead of quadratic communication cost. To keep the optimization running, each affected EV recovers locally with a certified, fleet-aware machine learning price forecast, and we prove that the optimization remains convergent with a recovery cost bounded by the shape of the forecast error. Simulation results with real-world load, price, and charging data show that a biased operator raises the annual cost of disadvantaged EVs by 132.7% and lowers that of advantaged EVs by 49.3% without changing the aggregate load, whereas the defense limits all cost changes to 2.6%. An external MITM attacker raises the cost of its victims by 57.6%, the peak load by 5.8%, and the grid cost by 15.8%, whereas the defense keeps them within 1.1%, 0.2%, and 0.3% of benign operation. With up to 70% of the EVs attacked, the recovery converges in at least 97.8% of the runs.
tldr: This paper proposes a Byzantine-resilient distributed EV charging coordination framework that combines threshold-signed broadcasts, upload recomputation, and machine-learning price forecasting to detect and recover from malicious participants in ADMM-based optimization.
motivation: Distributed ADMM-based EV charging coordination assumes all participants follow the algorithm, but biased operators, man-in-the-middle attackers, and compromised EVs can send inconsistent signals and silently degrade convergence, so a detection and recovery mechanism is needed.
method: The authors first prove that Byzantine attacks do not prevent ADMM convergence and derive the most damaging attack in closed form, then design a threshold-signed broadcast with upload recomputation for deviation detection at linear communication cost, plus a certified fleet-aware ML price forecast enabling local recovery.
result: Simulations on real load, price, and charging data show a biased operator raises disadvantaged EVs' annual cost by 132.7% and lowers advantaged EVs' by 49.3%, while the defense limits cost changes to 2.6%; an MITM attacker raises victim cost by 57.6% and grid cost by 15.8%, with the defense keeping deviations within ~1%, and recovery converging in at least 97.8% of runs with up to 70% of EVs attacked.
conclusion: Threshold cryptography combined with ML-based forecasting yields a fair, efficient, and Byzantine-resilient distributed EV charging coordination scheme with bounded recovery cost.

title: Erratum To Power Boundedness And Related Properties For Weighted Composition Operators On $\mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$, Journal Of Functional Analysis 288 (2025), 110745
authors: Vicente Asensio, Enrique Jord\'a, Thomas Kalmes
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As was kindly pointed out to us by S. Li, the proofs of Theorem 2.11 and Lemma 3.1 in our original paper contain errors that require modifications of the corresponding statements. We also correct a gap in the proof of Lemma 2.1, whose statement remains valid. Furthermore, we explain the consequences for several subsequent results and provide the necessary corrections to their statements and proofs.
tldr: An erratum correcting flawed proofs and statements in a pure functional-analysis paper on power boundedness of weighted composition operators acting on the Schwartz space S(R^d).
motivation: The authors were informed by S. Li that the proofs of Theorem 2.11 and Lemma 3.1 in their original Journal of Functional Analysis paper were erroneous, necessitating corrections.
method: The erratum revisits and patches the erroneous arguments, revises the affected theorem and lemma statements, and fills a gap in the proof of Lemma 2.1 (whose statement remains valid).
result: Corrected statements and proofs are supplied for Theorem 2.11, Lemma 3.1 and Lemma 2.1, together with an account of how subsequent results are affected.
conclusion: The original results are repaired with modified hypotheses/conclusions, but the work remains entirely within classical functional analysis with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Innovative Integrated Congestion Management Market: Synergizing Operational Flexibility Of Transmission System Operators With Aggregator-Driven Resources
authors: Arash Beiranvand
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces an innovative congestion management market that seeks to integrate and harness the operational flexibility available to Transmission System Operators (TSO) in conjunction with the flexibility offered by aggregators. In the context of operational flexibility, this study investigates Network Topology Optimization (NTO) as a pivotal strategy for to address the transmission network congestion, specifically through the strategic switching of certain buses. To achieve this, an N-1 secured NTO is formulated using a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) methodology. Concurrently, acknowledging the crucial and growing importance of aggregator-provided flexibility in congestion management, the paper presents a novel integrated congestion management market. In this framework, aggregators submit bids, and the TSO, taking into account these bids alongside the potential for the NTO, clears the market with the goal of minimizing the overall cost of congestion management. The proposed integrated market is constructed using a linear optimization model, ensuring its practical applicability in real world scenarios. The effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed market design are assessed using the standard IEEE 39-bus system, with results indicating promising potential and applicability.
tldr: The paper proposes an integrated congestion management market that combines transmission system operator network topology optimization with aggregator-provided flexibility.
motivation: Growing transmission congestion and the need to leverage both TSO operational flexibility and aggregator resources motivate a coordinated market design.
method: It formulates an N-1-secured network topology optimization using mixed-integer linear programming and constructs an integrated market clearing model as a linear optimization problem.
result: Case studies on the IEEE 39-bus system indicate promising potential and practical applicability of the proposed market design.
conclusion: The integrated market can harness TSO flexibility and aggregator bids to reduce congestion management costs, though the work is in power systems economics rather than quantum information.

title: Complete Center Classification Of A Quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-Equivariant System Via Rational Descent And Ramification
authors: Feng Li, Meilan Cai, Chaochao Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a new structural method to completely classify the elementary centers of a ten-parameter quintic [MATH]-equivariant system. The method overcomes the computational bottleneck of direct focus-quantity elimination by combining a Li\'enard reduction, a necessary-and-sufficient analytic involution criterion, and rational descent with residue and ramification analysis. We obtain forty-two explicit original-parameter conditions covering the entire center locus, including all degenerate and boundary cases. Sufficiency is established constructively through integrating factors, first integrals and explicit reversible realizations.
tldr: The paper develops a structural algebraic method to completely classify all elementary centers of a ten-parameter quintic Z2-equivariant planar polynomial differential system.
motivation: Direct focus-quantity elimination for high-parameter planar systems is computationally prohibitive, so a more tractable structural approach is needed to characterize the full center locus, including degenerate and boundary cases.
method: The authors combine a Liénard reduction, a necessary-and-sufficient analytic involution criterion, and rational descent with residue and ramification analysis to avoid brute-force elimination of focus quantities.
result: They obtain forty-two explicit original-parameter conditions covering the entire center locus, with sufficiency established constructively via integrating factors, first integrals, and explicit reversible realizations.
conclusion: The approach gives a complete and rigorous center classification for the quintic Z2-equivariant family and offers a general structural template for similar high-parameter equivariant systems.

title: An Accelerated Multiobjective Gradient Flow With Implicit Hessian-driven Damping
authors: Hao Luo Wen Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose an accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping for unconstrained convex multiobjective optimization problems in a real Hilbert space. The continuous flow is formulated as a system of two first-order equations involving only a single multiobjective projection operator and suitable time-scaling factors. Formally, it can also be expressed as a second-order system with explicit multiobjective Hessian-driven damping, which corresponds to the usual Hessian-driven damping introduced by Alvarez et al. [J. Math. Pures Appl., 81(8):747--779, 2002]. The first-order formulation, however, involves no Hessian term and can be regarded as an extension of the Hessian-driven Nesterov accelerated gradient flow by Chen and Luo [arXiv:1912.09276, 2019]. Assuming that the objective gradients are Lipschitz continuous on bounded sets and that the common lower level sets are bounded, we establish global existence in finite dimensions under suitable time-scaling conditions. An a priori energy estimate confines the solutions to a fixed bounded set, and a Lyapunov argument yields fast decay of a merit function and the KKT residual. Under an additional bound on the time-scaling factors, the trajectory of every global solution converges weakly to a weak Pareto point. Numerical tests illustrate the rapid residual decay and reduced oscillations.
tldr: The paper proposes an accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping for convex multiobjective optimization in Hilbert spaces.
motivation: It aims to accelerate convergence and reduce oscillations in multiobjective optimization by combining Hessian-driven damping with a first-order projective formulation.
method: The authors formulate a two-equation continuous flow using a single multiobjective projection operator and time-scaling factors, then analyze global existence, boundedness, Lyapunov decay, and convergence to weak Pareto points.
result: Under Lipschitz gradient and bounded lower-level-set assumptions, they prove global existence, fast decay of a merit function and KKT residual, and weak convergence of trajectories to weak Pareto points under an additional time-scaling bound.
conclusion: Numerical tests illustrate rapid residual decay and reduced oscillations, but the work is purely in convex multiobjective optimization and has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Auto-conditioned Gradient Descent Methods For Multiobjective Optimization
authors: Shuaichenji Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes two linesearch-free algorithms based on steepest descent methods for smooth multiobjective optimization: auto-conditioned steepest descent method for multiobjective optimization (AC-SDM) and auto-conditioned normalized gradient descent method for multiobjective optimization (AC-NGDM). Both algorithms estimate the local Lipschitz constant from the function values and the first-order information obtained in previous iterations. AC-SDM uses a shared estimate of the Lipschitz constant to construct a scaled steepest descent direction. For AC-NGDM, we use each function's local Lipschitz estimate to normalize the gradient of the corresponding function and construct the descent direction. We prove that every accumulation point of any sequence generated by both algorithms is a Pareto critical point. We also establish convergence rates of [MATH] for nonconvex objectives and [MATH] for convex objectives. Numerical results on several test problems demonstrate that AC-SDM and AC-NGDM require fewer iterations and less CPU time than the multiobjective steepest descent method with an Armijo line search and a max-type nonmonotone line search.
tldr: The paper introduces two line-search-free, auto-conditioned gradient descent algorithms (AC-SDM and AC-NGDM) for smooth multiobjective optimization that estimate local Lipschitz constants on the fly.
motivation: Multiobjective steepest descent methods typically rely on line searches (e.g., Armijo or nonmonotone max-type), which add per-iteration cost and tuning burden; the authors aim to eliminate this by self-tuning the step size from observed function and gradient information.
method: AC-SDM uses a single shared Lipschitz-constant estimate to build a scaled steepest-descent direction, while AC-NGDM uses per-objective estimates to normalize each gradient component; both adaptively refine their estimates from previous iterations' function values and first-order information.
result: Both algorithms are proven to converge to Pareto critical points, with rates of order 1/epsilon^2 for nonconvex objectives and faster rates for convex ones, and numerical tests show fewer iterations and lower CPU time than Armijo and max-type nonmonotone line-search baselines.
conclusion: Auto-conditioned, line-search-free descent provides a practical and theoretically sound alternative for multiobjective optimization, though the work lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: High-order Imex Local Discontinuous Galerkin Methods With Sparse Grids For High-dimensional Nonlinear Parabolic PDEs
authors: Joel P. Villarino, Manuel J. Castro, J. A. Garc\'ia-Rodr\'iguez, J. G. L\'opez-Salas
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a high-order IMEX-LDG scheme on sparse grids for solving nonlinear parabolic PDEs in moderate to high dimensions. The method combines the advantages of LDG methods for convection--diffusion problems, IMEX-RK time integrators for stiff systems, and sparse-grid techniques to mitigate the curse of dimensionality. The resulting scheme is fully parallelized in MPI, is robust, efficient, and scalable, making it suitable for a wide range of applications involving high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDEs.
tldr: The paper introduces a high-order IMEX local discontinuous Galerkin scheme on sparse grids for solving high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDEs efficiently.
motivation: Solving nonlinear parabolic PDEs in moderate to high dimensions is hindered by the curse of dimensionality and stiffness, motivating schemes that combine high-order accuracy with dimensional reduction.
method: The authors couple LDG spatial discretization for convection-diffusion problems with IMEX Runge-Kutta time integrators, and use sparse-grid techniques plus MPI parallelization to reduce cost.
result: The resulting scheme is reported to be robust, efficient, and scalable, mitigating the curse of dimensionality while retaining high-order accuracy.
conclusion: The method provides a practical, parallelizable numerical framework broadly applicable to high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDE problems.

title: On The Same Track: Privacy Leaks In Electric Rail Transport Via Magnetic Fields
authors: Stefan Czybik, Pia Hanfeld, Konrad Rieck
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inertial sensors of smartphones are a well-known privacy risk, as they allow inferring sensitive user movements and activity without explicit permissions. Among these sensors, the magnetometer has received little attention, as it is assumed to measure mainly the Earth's magnetic field. In this paper, we show that electric trains generate distinctive magnetic fields that can be captured by a smartphone magnetometer. Apps deployed on the device can access these signals without user permission, enabling two novel attacks on passenger privacy: First, we are able to determine whether the user is riding an electric train (transport mode detection). Second, we can infer whether other victims are aboard the same train due to shared patterns in the magnetic field (colocation prediction). In an empirical evaluation across 217 train rides, we demonstrate that both attacks are effective, confirming a real-world threat. We discuss countermeasures and argue that magnetometer access should require explicit user permission in mobile operating systems.
tldr: The paper shows that smartphone magnetometers can detect distinctive magnetic-field signatures from electric trains, enabling transport-mode detection and colocation prediction without user permission.
motivation: Inertial smartphone sensors pose privacy risks, but the magnetometer is often assumed to measure mainly Earth's magnetic field and has received little attention as a leakage channel.
method: The authors collect magnetometer measurements across 217 train rides and analyze magnetic-field patterns to detect whether a user is on an electric train and whether other victims are on the same train.
result: Both attacks are empirically effective, demonstrating a real-world privacy threat from unpermissioned magnetometer access on mobile devices.
conclusion: The work argues that mobile operating systems should require explicit user permission for magnetometer access and discusses possible countermeasures.

title: Counting Second-Order Schreier Sets With Minimum 2
authors: Dongho Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A finite nonempty set [MATH] is (first-order) Schreier if [MATH]. These Schreier sets can be generalized recursively to higher-order Schreier sets, and we specifically investigate the second-order Schreier sets. We show that the count of second-order Schreier sets with minimum element [MATH] and maximum element [MATH] is one more than the [MATH] term of the convolution of the Fibonacci numbers [MATH] with [MATH] (given by Sequence A023610 in the OEIS).
tldr: The paper counts second-order Schreier sets by minimum and maximum element, expressing the count via a convolution of Fibonacci numbers related to OEIS sequence A023610.
motivation: Schreier sets and their higher-order generalizations are combinatorial objects with connections to Banach space theory and Ramsey-type constructions; the author aims to enumerate a specific class of second-order Schreier sets.
method: The paper uses recursive definitions of higher-order Schreier sets and combinatorial counting arguments to derive a formula involving Fibonacci-number convolutions.
result: For second-order Schreier sets with minimum m and maximum M, the count is one plus a term in the convolution of Fibonacci numbers, identified with OEIS A023610.
conclusion: The work provides an explicit combinatorial enumeration result for second-order Schreier sets, linking them to known Fibonacci convolution sequences.

title: A Unified Framework For First- And Second-Order Energy-Stable Parametric Finite Element Methods For Planar Willmore Flow
authors: Yujing Yan Xiaoli Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The construction of structure-preserving schemes for planar Willmore flow that are second-order accurate in time and avoid large coupled nonlinear solves remains challenging. In this work, we develop a unified framework for first- and second-order fully discrete energy-stable parametric finite element schemes for planar Willmore flow with a length-penalization term. The framework is based on a new equivalent reformulation involving a global auxiliary variable. The main novelty lies in the second-order construction, which combines midpoint curvature quantities weighted by elementwise arc-length Jacobian ratios with a compatible discrete tangent to obtain exact discrete chain rules for the bending energy and curve length. A further contribution is to show that both schemes satisfy discrete modified energy dissipation laws that yield the same type of a priori bounds on the discrete solution as the original energy law. They also retain Barrett--Garcke--N{\"u}rnberg tangential motion to promote favorable mesh distribution. Each stage reduces to two linear solves with exactly the same coefficient matrix and one scalar nonlinear solve. We rigorously prove unique solvability of the linear subproblems under suitable assumptions and derive computable sufficient conditions for local existence and uniqueness of the scalar solution near unity. Numerical experiments demonstrate the expected temporal accuracy, energy dissipation, good mesh quality and computational efficiency.
tldr: The paper develops a unified framework for first- and second-order energy-stable parametric finite element schemes for planar Willmore flow with a length-penalization term.
motivation: Constructing structure-preserving schemes for planar Willmore flow that are second-order accurate in time while avoiding large coupled nonlinear solves remains challenging.
method: The authors introduce a new equivalent reformulation with a global auxiliary variable, and build the second-order scheme from midpoint curvature quantities weighted by elementwise arc-length Jacobian ratios plus a compatible discrete tangent, giving exact discrete chain rules for bending energy and curve length.
result: Both schemes satisfy discrete modified energy dissipation laws yielding a priori bounds, retain Barrett-Garcke-Nurnberg tangential motion, and each stage reduces to two linear solves sharing one coefficient matrix plus one scalar nonlinear solve; unique solvability and local existence conditions are proven and numerics confirm expected accuracy.
conclusion: The framework provides efficient, energy-stable, second-order accurate finite element methods for planar Willmore flow with good mesh quality, but it lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: Online Carbon-Aware Power Flexibility Quantification Of Distributed Data Centers
authors: Yue Chen Xiaowei Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geographically distributed data centers (DCs) can provide spatio-temporal power flexibility to electric grids through the coordinated management of computing resources and energy. Beyond their energy consumption, the carbon footprints of DCs are non-negligible, which constrain the power flexibility that DCs can offer to the power grid. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a carbon-aware power flexibility quantification framework for DCs. We first develop an optimization model that characterizes DC power flexibility in a grid-usable form, namely the Cartesian product of adjustable power demand intervals across time slots. An online algorithm based on Lyapunov optimization is then designed to solve the flexibility quantification model in real time under uncertain workload arrivals and fluctuating grid carbon intensity. Furthermore, an integrated disaggregation and feedback mechanism is devised to translate the power system operator's dispatch commands into real-time DC operating decisions and to capture their impact on future DC flexibility. Several desirable properties of the proposed model and method are proven, including disaggregation feasibility, bounded workload processing delays, and a bounded suboptimality gap. Numerical simulations demonstrate that our approach effectively unlocks DC power flexibility while satisfying carbon emission constraints, outperforming baseline algorithms.
tldr: The paper proposes a carbon-aware framework for quantifying the spatio-temporal power flexibility that geographically distributed data centers can offer to electric grids, using an online Lyapunov-optimization algorithm.
motivation: Distributed data centers can supply valuable power flexibility to the grid, but their carbon footprints constrain how much flexibility they can actually provide, creating a need for carbon-aware quantification methods.
method: The authors formulate an optimization model that expresses DC flexibility as a Cartesian product of adjustable power-demand intervals over time slots, solve it online via Lyapunov optimization under uncertain workload arrivals and fluctuating grid carbon intensity, and add a disaggregation/feedback mechanism linking operator dispatch commands to real-time DC operations.
result: They prove disaggregation feasibility, bounded workload processing delays, and a bounded suboptimality gap, and simulations show the approach unlocks DC power flexibility under carbon constraints while outperforming baselines.
conclusion: The framework enables data centers to participate in grid flexibility markets while respecting emission limits, though the work lies entirely in power-systems scheduling and has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-probability Convergence Of Adaptive, Proximal, And Clipped Adam-type Methods For Nonconvex Stochastic Optimization
authors: Zhongyi Huang Xiaopeng Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a unified high-probability analysis of adaptive, proximal, and clipped first-order methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization. For a smooth objective whose stochastic gradient error has sub-Gaussian norm, the normalized adaptive gradient method attains the standard stochastic nonconvex complexity of the square root of the number of iterations, with an additional logarithmic dependence on the inverse confidence level that is inversely proportional to the number of iterations. The proof uses an adaptive descent decomposition together with Freedman and Bernstein concentration inequalities. The same guarantee is established for the full adaptive moment method under an explicit momentum-alignment condition. The analysis is extended to projected and proximal updates through a stationarity measure based on the subdifferential distance, to objectives satisfying the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, and to heavy-tailed noise through truncation. The framework is applied to stochastic inverse problems in elasticity, and numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical scaling and the practical behavior of the methods.
tldr: This paper develops high-probability convergence guarantees for adaptive, proximal, and clipped Adam-type methods in nonconvex stochastic optimization.
motivation: The work aims to provide a unified theoretical analysis of popular first-order optimization methods under realistic noise assumptions, including heavy-tailed noise and proximal/constrained settings.
method: It uses adaptive descent decompositions together with Freedman and Bernstein concentration inequalities to derive high-probability bounds for normalized adaptive gradient and Adam-type updates.
result: The analysis recovers standard stochastic nonconvex complexity with logarithmic confidence dependence, extends to proximal/projected updates, Polyak-Lojasiewicz objectives, and heavy-tailed noise via truncation.
conclusion: The framework is applied to stochastic inverse problems in elasticity and supported by numerical experiments illustrating the theoretical scaling and practical behavior.

title: The Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz Paper: A 10-Year Retrospective
authors: Hamed Karimi, Julie Nutini, Mark Schmidt
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2016, we wrote a paper introducing the phrase "Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition" for an old idea, unsure of how readers would react. The paper ultimately had a larger impact than we expected, and we are surprised and honoured to receive the 2026 PKDD ECML Test of Time Award. With 10 years of hindsight, this note offers an informal and candid retrospective on the PL condition. We take a look back at the origins of the paper, give an AI-assisted refined version of the main theorem, review criticisms of the work, and discuss a variety of related ideas and extensions.
tldr: A ten-year retrospective on the 2016 paper that popularized the term 'Polyak-Łojasiewicz (PL) condition' for analyzing gradient-based optimization convergence.
motivation: The authors revisit their influential optimization paper upon receiving a test-of-time award, aiming to candidly recount its origins, reception, criticisms, and subsequent extensions.
method: An informal retrospective note that recounts the paper's history, presents an AI-assisted refined statement and proof of the main theorem, and surveys critical feedback and related developments.
result: The note clarifies the PL condition's role as a sufficient condition for gradient-descent convergence without convexity, restates the main theorem in refined form, and catalogues extensions and critiques accumulated over a decade.
conclusion: The PL condition has proven to be a widely useful analytical tool in nonconvex optimization; the authors reflect on its unexpected impact and outline remaining open questions.

title: Statistical Guarantees For Signature Kernel Ridge Regression
authors: Jakob Kellermann Christian Bayer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Path signatures are a standard tool for learning functionals on path space. The main underpinnings of their application are universal approximation results. For a wide range of function classes on path space, these results state that any function in such a class can be approximated arbitrarily well by a linear functional of the path signature. Hence, linear functionals of the signature are in principle expressive enough for learning functions on path space. Nonetheless, these results do not provide insights into the statistical question of how much data is needed to identify a suitable signature functional. In this work, we study this question in the framework of kernel ridge regression with the signature kernel. The target is the conditional expectation [MATH], where [MATH] is the observed path and [MATH] is a real-valued response. Under different assumptions on the moments of the signature kernel and the response, we provide finite-sample and consistency guarantees for the method. We supplement our theoretical analysis with numerical experiments that illustrate our results.
tldr: The paper provides finite-sample and consistency guarantees for kernel ridge regression using path signatures to learn conditional expectations on path space.
motivation: Path signatures are expressive for functionals on path space, but universal approximation results do not address how much data is needed to learn a suitable signature functional.
method: The authors analyze kernel ridge regression with the signature kernel, deriving statistical guarantees under moment assumptions on the signature kernel and response variable, supplemented by numerical experiments.
result: They establish finite-sample and consistency guarantees for the signature-kernel regression estimator under different moment conditions.
conclusion: The work gives statistical learning guarantees for signature-based regression, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Bound-preserving Finite Volume Scheme For A Coupled Parabolic System With Nonlinear And Nonlocal Drift
authors: Adrian Muntean Nicklas J\"averg{\aa}rd
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a bound preserving finite-volume scheme for a coupled system of partial differential equations with nonlinear, nonlocal drift. The main contribution of this work is twofold: [MATH] we show that the proposed scheme preserves physically motivated bounds; [MATH] we prove that the scheme is well-posed and leads to a sequence of approximate solutions converging to the weak solution of the original problem. This setting is motivated by questions related to morphology formation in organic solar cells.
tldr: The authors construct a bound-preserving finite-volume scheme for a coupled parabolic PDE system with nonlinear nonlocal drift and prove its convergence to a weak solution.
motivation: Such coupled drift-diffusion systems arise in modeling morphology formation in organic solar cells, where physically meaningful bounds on densities must be respected numerically.
method: A finite-volume discretization is proposed that provably preserves the physically motivated bounds; well-posedness of the scheme and convergence of the approximate solutions to the weak solution of the continuous problem are established.
result: The scheme is shown to be well-posed and bound-preserving, and the sequence of approximate solutions is proven to converge to a weak solution of the original coupled parabolic system.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous numerical foundation for simulating coupled parabolic systems with nonlocal drift, motivated by organic solar cell morphology modeling.

title: Singularly Embedded Solitons And Stokes Phenomenon In The Fifth Order KdV Equation
authors: Roberto Barrio, Vassili Gelfreich, J. Tom\'as L\'azaro, Juan Ramon Pacha
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study embedded solitons (ES) in a fifth-order Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation near a reversible Hamiltonian saddle-centre bifurcation. The solitons correspond to homoclinic orbits to an equilibrium whose linearisation has a pair of real and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. Existence of symmetric homoclinic near the bifurcation is a codimension-one phenomenon governed by a parameter-dependent Stokes constant associated with an inner equation. Using complex matching, we derive an oscillatory large-parameter asymptotic formula for the Stokes constant. This formula implies the existence of a countable sequence of zeros and gives their asymptotic distribution in parameter space. We also develop two complementary high-precision numerical procedures for evaluating the Stokes constant: one based on the late terms of the formal inner expansion and another on direct computation of the stable and unstable manifolds. The numerical results agree with each other and with the asymptotic prediction, confirming both the existence and the predicted locations of the embedded-soliton branches.
tldr: A rigorous asymptotic and numerical study of embedded solitons in the fifth-order KdV equation, characterized via exponentially small Stokes constants near a reversible Hamiltonian saddle-centre bifurcation.
motivation: Embedded solitons in higher-order KdV models are non-generic homoclinic structures whose existence is controlled by exponentially small effects, requiring beyond-all-orders asymptotics to locate and count solution branches.
method: The authors use complex matching to derive an oscillatory large-parameter asymptotic formula for the Stokes constant of the inner equation, complemented by two high-precision numerical schemes: one using late terms of the formal inner expansion and one computing stable/unstable manifolds directly.
result: The asymptotic formula predicts a countable sequence of zeros of the Stokes constant with a definite distribution in parameter space; numerics confirm both the predicted locations and the existence of the embedded-soliton branches.
conclusion: The work provides a quantitative theory of embedded solitons in fifth-order KdV, demonstrating agreement between asymptotics and numerics and giving a systematic method for locating such solutions.

title: Muon Attains $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ Iteration Complexity Under Shuffling
authors: Kun Huang, Shi Pu, Karl Henrik Johansson
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Muon is a stochastic first-order optimizer for matrix-valued parameters. It maintains an exponential moving average of stochastic gradients in a momentum buffer with coefficient [MATH], and orthogonalizes the buffer to obtain the update direction. Muon has been reported to accelerate and stabilize the training of large language models. In practice, it is often used with shuffling (sampling without replacement), where each epoch visits the components of a finite-sum objective in a permuted order. However, its iteration complexity in this setting remains open. We analyze Muon under shuffling, with the momentum buffer orthogonalized by the polar map. For smooth nonconvex finite-sum problems, we establish an [MATH] iteration complexity for finding an [MATH]-stationary point. This guarantee holds for every sequence of permutations, covering random reshuffling, shuffle once, and the incremental gradient method. This complexity matches that of stochastic gradient descent under shuffling in its dependence on [MATH], and improves on Muon's [MATH] complexity under sampling with replacement. Our guarantee requires a problem-dependent [MATH] that approaches one as the number of components grows. In contrast, no fixed [MATH] guarantees convergence to stationarity for every number of components. We show this by constructing a family of smooth convex problems on which, for any fixed [MATH], Muon remains bounded away from stationarity once the number of components is sufficiently large. This failure occurs for every sequence of permutations and persists even with small stepsizes. These results suggest two practical tuning rules: if the training loss stops decreasing even after reducing the stepsize, increase [MATH]; when increasing [MATH], reduce the stepsize accordingly.
tldr: This paper establishes an O(ε^-3) iteration complexity for the Muon optimizer under shuffling (sampling without replacement) on smooth nonconvex finite-sum problems, and constructs counterexamples showing convergence can fail for fixed problem-dependent parameters as the number of components grows.
motivation: Muon is widely used with shuffling to train large language models, but its iteration complexity in this regime was unknown; prior guarantees either assumed with-replacement sampling or gave weaker epsilon dependence.
method: The authors analyze Muon with a momentum buffer orthogonalized via the polar map, prove a uniform complexity bound valid for every permutation sequence (random reshuffling, shuffle once, incremental gradient), and build a family of smooth convex problems to demonstrate failure modes of fixed-parameter variants.
result: They obtain O(ε^-3) complexity matching shuffled SGD's ε-dependence and improving Muon's O(ε^-4) with-replacement bound, contingent on a problem-dependent constant approaching one as the number of components grows; for any fixed constant they show Muon can stay bounded away from stationarity regardless of stepsize.
conclusion: The results yield practical tuning guidance (increase the parameter and decrease stepsize when training loss stalls) and clarify the theoretical role of shuffling for matrix-valued momentum optimizers.

title: Sample Complexity And Scalability Of Adaptive-sampling Trust-region Methods For Zeroth-order Stochastic Optimization --- Part~II: A New Pathwise Analysis With Randomized Subspaces
authors: Sara Shashaani, Coralia Cartis, Kwassi Joseph Dzahini
abstract: ArXiv:2611.18174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic trust-region methods are usually analyzed in expectation or with high probability: the guarantee is about the law of the algorithm, not about the run in hand. This paper analyzes the adaptive sampling stochastic trust-region method ASTRO-DF (which is the reuse variant ASTRA-R in Part I) in random subspaces along almost every sample path. The route has one probabilistic ingredient, the accuracy of the common-random-number estimates at the adaptive sample size, uniformly over the trust region; Part~I established it by chaining, here it is obtained at the stopping time by optional stopping and converted, by the first Borel--Cantelli lemma, into an accuracy that holds from a random index on, after which the deterministic trust-region argument applies. We prove almost sure convergence and almost sure iteration and sample complexity of orders [MATH] and [MATH], with a subspace dimension growing logarithmically; we show that at a fixed subspace dimension the eventual-accuracy argument yields [MATH] iterations and [MATH] samples; we show that the random index after which the rates hold cannot be too large and has an explicit, rapidly decaying tail. Compared with the supermartingale route, the pathwise route needs no lower bound on the per-iteration probability of a good iteration, no coupling between the trust-region expansion factor and the sketch, and no moment condition on the summed squared radii.
tldr: A pathwise (almost-sure) analysis of the adaptive-sampling stochastic trust-region method ASTRO-DF/ASTRA-R using randomized subspaces, establishing almost-sure convergence and iteration/sample complexity bounds.
motivation: Standard analyses of stochastic trust-region methods guarantee properties in expectation or with high probability about the algorithm's law rather than the individual run; the authors seek run-in-hand, pathwise guarantees.
method: They obtain uniform accuracy of common-random-number gradient estimates at the adaptive sample size via optional stopping at the stopping time, convert it to eventual accuracy using the first Borel–Cantelli lemma, then apply a deterministic trust-region argument in random subspaces of logarithmically growing dimension.
result: They prove almost-sure convergence and almost-sure iteration and sample complexity of stated orders, show fixed-subspace-dimension rates, and derive an explicit, rapidly decaying tail bound on the random index after which the rates hold.
conclusion: The pathwise route avoids needing a lower bound on good-iteration probability, coupling between expansion factor and sketch, or moment conditions, offering a cleaner alternative to the supermartingale approach.

title: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? An Empirical Security Study Of Weight-Space Programming
authors: Zhaojia Wang, Jiucui Lu, Zheng Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in weight-space programming (WSP) have demonstrated that large language models (LLMs) can directly inspect and modify neural network weights without conventional gradient-based training. While this capability opens new possibilities for model improvement, it also raises an important security question: Can LLMs exploit weight-space programming to inject backdoors into neural networks? To answer this question, we present an empirical security study of LLM-driven weight-space programming for backdoor injection. Specifically, we investigate whether general-purpose LLMs can directly modify the weights of target models according to natural-language instructions, without accessing task-specific data, performing forward passes, or computing gradients. We evaluate five LLMs as weight editors across three target architectures: an MLP on MNIST, ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on AG News. Our experiments reveal three key findings. First, LLM-driven weight editing can successfully inject backdoors across different architectures while largely preserving clean performance. Second, successful attacks can require remarkably few parameter modifications, including only six parameters for the MLP and 0.02% of the weights for a fine-tuned Qwen model. Third, editing capabilities vary substantially across LLMs and target architectures: although all five LLMs successfully backdoor the MLP, only GPT-6 Astra succeeds across all three targets. These findings highlight an emerging security risk of weight-space programming and underscore the importance of safeguarding LLM-driven weight editing.
tldr: An empirical security study showing that general-purpose LLMs can inject backdoors into neural networks by directly editing weights via natural-language instructions, without data, gradients, or forward passes.
motivation: Weight-space programming lets LLMs inspect and modify neural network weights directly, which raises the question of whether this capability can be abused to implant backdoors in target models.
method: Five LLMs act as weight editors on three targets (an MLP for MNIST, ResNet-18 for CIFAR-10, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct for AG News), editing parameters per textual instructions with no task data, forward passes, or gradients.
result: Backdoors can be injected across architectures while largely preserving clean accuracy, sometimes with as few as six parameters (MLP) or 0.02% of weights (Qwen), though editing success varies strongly across models and targets.
conclusion: LLM-driven weight editing constitutes an emerging security risk that motivates safeguards on weight-space programming tools.

title: Continuous Cuffless Blood Pressure Estimation Using Ppg From Methods To Clinical Translation
authors: Karthika Shalini Potail, Harshitha Manjunatha, Hetvi Kotadia, Tooraj Nikoubin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.17499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous blood pressure (BP) monitoring could improve hypertension management by capturing changes that intermittent cuff measurements miss. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is widely explored for cuffless BP estimation because optical sensors are inexpensive, wearable, and already present in many consumer and clinical devices. PPG, however, does not measure arterial pressure: BP is inferred from waveform characteristics or pulse timing, which also depend on vascular tone, arterial stiffness, sensor contact, motion, and individual physiology. This survey reviews PPG-based cuffless BP estimation along the full measurement chain, covering physiological mechanisms, waveform features, pulse arrival time (PAT), pulse transit time (PTT), machine-learning methods, datasets, calibration, validation, deployment, bias, and clinical translation. Studies are assessed by the strength of evidence they provide rather than by reported error alone, with particular attention to subject and temporal leakage, dataset imbalance, calibration dependence and drift, motion artifacts, and the gap between benchmark accuracy and reliable real-world measurement. The review finds that progress depends on more than better prediction algorithms. Future work should prioritize physiologically informed models, diverse longitudinal datasets, transparent reporting of calibration requirements and failure rates, stronger evaluation protocols, and studies that demonstrate practical value in clinical care.
tldr: A survey of photoplethysmography-based cuffless blood pressure estimation covering physiological mechanisms, signal features, machine learning, datasets, calibration, and clinical translation challenges.
motivation: Continuous blood pressure monitoring could improve hypertension management beyond intermittent cuff measurements, and PPG sensors are cheap, wearable, and widely deployed, motivating a critical review of the field.
method: The authors survey the full measurement chain — physiology, waveform features, pulse arrival/transit time, ML methods, datasets, calibration, validation, deployment, and bias — and assess studies by strength of evidence rather than reported error alone.
result: The review identifies pervasive issues such as subject and temporal leakage, dataset imbalance, calibration dependence and drift, motion artifacts, and a gap between benchmark accuracy and real-world reliability.
conclusion: Progress requires physiologically informed models, diverse longitudinal datasets, transparent reporting of calibration and failure rates, stronger evaluation protocols, and demonstrated clinical value rather than better prediction algorithms alone.
